The primary claim is this recipe-scoped $T$ vs.\ non-text intervenability asymmetry---intervention accessibili

89858b4c7d656c59fe2576eb.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20298v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Type systems are a lightweight way to obtain formal assurance that code upholds security properties. However, decentralized systems, such as smart contracts and Model Context Protocol ecosystems, have limited ability to constrain the behavior of untrusted code. In such systems, attackers may attempt to confuse trusted code by supplying values that do not behave according to their advertised types, an attack that we call type confusion. Well-known attacks such as confused deputy attacks, reentrancy attacks, and control-flow hijacking can be understood as instances of type confusion. We define type confusion security as the property that unrestricted attackers who need not follow the type system have no more power than limited attackers who fully obey it. We formally define type confusion security as a real--ideal emulation, and in the context of an information-flow-typed core calculus that statically enforces security against well-typed attackers, prove that its run-time checks also enforce security against ill-typed attackers. In this system, programmers can write code while reasoning about security only against well-typed attackers; the security guarantees enforced by the type system still hold. We mechanize a proof of type confusion security in Lean.

58546e6c2c9da72aacf0a55a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Taint analysis for C depends on how precisely the analysis tracks tainted values as they flow through memory objects. Without field sensitivity, a tainted object field can spuriously taint an entire object, producing significant false alarms. In this paper, we present a field-sensitive taint analysis that combines Data Structure Analysis (DSA) for field-sensitive points-to information with a data-flow analysis for tracking explicit dependencies. We identify that existing DSA-style analyses lose precision on a common object pattern: a C struct object that mixes scalar fields with a flexible array member. When such an array is accessed with symbolic indices, DSA loses points-to field sensitivity for the entire object, inflating false alarms in the data-flow analysis. To address this, we propose I-DSA, which extends DSA by representing field positions as intervals, so that a pointer with symbolic bounds merges only the fields within those bounds. We further develop a sound data-flow analysis based on abstract interpretation. We implement I-DSA on top of SeaDSA and the data-flow analysis inside Crab. Our tool targets LLVM IR and supports configurable taint policies by instrumenting the IR with taint intrinsics. Our experiments show that I-DSA reduces the false alarms caused by this pattern at little cost in the pointer analysis, that SVF, an inclusion-based pointer analysis, shows a similar field-sensitivity loss, and that our tai

3ebb5c022acd2d35e43096bc.title_original: K-out-of-N Oblivious Transfer over Erasure Channels: Capacity and Reductions
3ebb5c022acd2d35e43096bc.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21359v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study $K$-out-of-$N$ oblivious transfer (OT) between a server and a client over a discrete memoryless channel, under an honest-but-curious model. The client must retrieve $K$ out of $N$ messages stored by the server while learning nothing about the remaining $N-K$ messages, and the server must not learn the client's selection. For a binary erasure channel (BEC) with parameter $\epsilon$, we show that the $K$-out-of-$N$ OT capacity is $\min\Big(\frac{K\epsilon}{N-K},1-\epsilon\Big)$. This characterization generalizes the known capacity results for $1$-out-of-$2$ OT and for $1$-out-of-$N$ OT when $\epsilon\ge\tfrac{N-1}{N}$. We also investigate OT reductions, specifically, we show that constructing a $K$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol from repeating $K$ times an optimal $1$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol can be suboptimal, but we also identify certain ranges of $\epsilon$ and $M < N$ for which a $1$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol can be optimally realized via the repetition of a $1$-out-of-$M$ OT protocol. Finally, we discuss extensions of our results to a generalized erasure channel (GEC).

63fa53277171418ea787ca97.title_original: ExclaveFL: Verifiable Claims for Federated Learning using Exclaves
63fa53277171418ea787ca97.excerpt: arXiv:2412.10537v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In federated learning (FL), data providers jointly train a machine learning model without sharing training data. This makes it challenging to provide verifiable claims about the trained model, e.g., related to the employed training data, data sanitization, or training algorithm---a malicious data provider can simply deviate from the correct training protocol without detection. Prior FL training systems have used trusted execution environments (TEEs) to protect the training computation, relying on the confidentiality and integrity of TEEs. TEE confidentiality, however, has been shown to be vulnerable to various attacks, e.g., via side channels. We describe ExclaveFL, a system for training FL models that establishes verifiable claims about models through fine-grained runtime attestation proofs. Since such proofs only require integrity, ExclaveFL generates them using exclaves, which are integrity-only execution environments without software-managed secrets, making them immune to data leakage attacks. ExclaveFL uses exclaves to attest data transformations during FL training, and the runtime attestation proofs then form an attested dataflow graph of the entire training computation. The graph is checked by an auditor to ensure that the trained model satisfies claims, e.g., about the use of data sanitization by data providers or aggregation by the model provider. Since exclaves require minor yet proprietary firmware changes, we eva

301ec6380c61746a8c8b68c5.title_original: LiteLMGuard: Seamless and Lightweight On-Device Guardrails for Small Language Models against Quantization Vulnerabilities
301ec6380c61746a8c8b68c5.excerpt: arXiv:2505.05619v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The growing adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) has influenced the development of Small Language Models (SLMs) for on-device deployment across smartphones and edge devices, offering enhanced privacy, reduced latency, server-free functionality, and improved user experience. However, due to on-device resource constraints, SLMs undergo size optimization through compression techniques like quantization, which inadvertently introduce fairness, ethical and privacy risks. Critically, quantized SLMs may respond to harmful queries directly, without requiring adversarial manipulation, raising significant safety and trust concerns. To address this, we propose LiteLMGuard, an on-device guardrail that provides real-time, prompt-level defense for quantized SLMs. Additionally, our guardrail is designed to be model-agnostic such that it can be seamlessly integrated with any SLM, operating independently of underlying architectures. Our LiteLMGuard formalizes deep learning (DL)-based prompt filtering by leveraging semantic understanding to classify prompt answerability for SLMs. Built on our curated Answerable-or-Not dataset, LiteLMGuard employs ELECTRA as the candidate model with 97.75% answerability classification accuracy. The on-device deployment of LiteLMGuard enabled real-time offline filtering with over 85% defense-rate against harmful prompts (including jailbreak attacks), 94% filtering accuracy and ~135 ms average latency. These

02ae01d288b8eba538c95fff.title_original: BitBypass: A New Direction in Jailbreaking Aligned Large Language Models with Bitstream Camouflage
02ae01d288b8eba538c95fff.excerpt: arXiv:2506.02479v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The inherent risk of generating harmful and unsafe content by Large Language Models (LLMs), has highlighted the need for their safety alignment. Various techniques like supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, and red-teaming were developed for ensuring the safety alignment of LLMs. However, the robustness of these aligned LLMs is always challenged by adversarial attacks that exploit unexplored and underlying vulnerabilities of the safety alignment. In this paper, we develop a novel black-box jailbreak attack, called BitBypass, that leverages hyphen-separated bitstream camouflage for jailbreaking aligned LLMs. This represents a new direction in jailbreaking by exploiting fundamental information representation of data as continuous bits, rather than leveraging prompt engineering or adversarial manipulations. Our evaluation of five state-of-the-art LLMs, namely GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5, Claude 3.5, Llama 3.1, and Mixtral, in adversarial perspective, revealed the capabilities of BitBypass in bypassing their safety alignment and tricking them into generating harmful and unsafe content. Further, we observed that BitBypass outperforms several state-of-the-art jailbreak attacks in terms of stealthiness and attack success. Overall, these results highlights the effectiveness and efficiency of BitBypass in jailbreaking these state-of-the-art LLMs.

bcbcfaa076835f2160dfb9b5.title_original: Vectorised Hashing Based on Bernstein-Rabin-Winograd Polynomials over Prime Order Fields
bcbcfaa076835f2160dfb9b5.excerpt: arXiv:2507.06490v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the new AXU hash function decBRWHash, which is parameterised by the positive integer $c$ and is based on Bernstein-Rabin-Winograd (BRW) polynomials. Choosing $c>1$ gives a hash function which can be implemented using $c$-way single instruction multiple data (SIMD) instructions. We report a set of very comprehensive hand optimised assembly implementations of 4-decBRWHash using avx2 SIMD instructions available on modern Intel processors. For comparison, we also report similar carefully optimised avx2 assembly implementations of polyHash, an AXU hash function based on usual polynomials. Our implementations are over prime order fields, specifically the primes $2^{127}-1$ and $2^{130}-5$. For the prime $2^{130}-5$, for avx2 implementations, compared to the famous Poly1305 hash function, 4-decBRWHash is faster for messages which are a few hundred bytes long and achieves a speed-up of about 16% for message lengths in a few kilobytes range and improves to a speed-up of about 23% for message lengths in a few megabytes range.

f1fe2c31cbdc6a5244eb7be2.title_original: DeepfakeBench-MM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Deepfake Detection
f1fe2c31cbdc6a5244eb7be2.excerpt: arXiv:2510.22622v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subjec

68079a3f05fa18e842ff4757.title_original: Mind the Gap: Cross-RFC Formal Analysis Exposes DNSSEC's Hidden Vulnerabilities
68079a3f05fa18e842ff4757.excerpt: arXiv:2512.11431v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a cross-RFC formal analysis of selected DNSSEC mechanisms using SAPIC+ models of cryptographic operations and stateful caching. We analyze properties concerning data origin authenticity, integrity, chain of trust, and authenticated denial of existence within these models. Our analysis shows that core authentication properties hold under the modeled assumptions, while wildcard expansion, the mechanism that bridges positive and negative authentication, exhibits a cross-RFC interaction vulnerability that defeats DNSSEC's integrity guarantee. Specifically, we discover Cross-Zone Wildcard Cache Poisoning: a new attack in which a malicious zone operator exploits a gap in the DNSSEC specifications to poison resolver caches with forged records for some domains outside its authority, served to clients as DNSSEC-authentic. The tested versions of all four major resolvers implementing the affected caching optimization accept the malformed wildcard material. The resulting impact depends on the resolver's synthesis path. All four vendors have publicly released fixes. The distinctive integrity failure is a synthesized, attacker-chosen positive answer with the Authenticated Data (AD) bit set: prior attacks instead exhausted availability, downgraded to AD=0, or skipped validation. Our models also identify two cross-RFC availability flaws and rediscover three known attack classes. We test six resolvers and measure deployme

2e8add184cd7a6ff04fc56ab.title_original: Better Call Graphs: A New Dataset of Function Call Graphs for Malware Classification
2e8add184cd7a6ff04fc56ab.excerpt: arXiv:2512.20872v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Function call graphs (FCGs) have emerged as a powerful abstraction for malware detection, capturing the behavioral structure of applications beyond surface-level signatures. Their utility in traditional program analysis has been well established, enabling effective classification and analysis of malicious software. In the mobile domain, especially in the Android ecosystem, FCG-based malware classification is particularly critical due to the platform's widespread adoption and the complex, component-based structure of Android apps. However, progress in this direction is hindered by the lack of large-scale, high-quality Android-specific FCG datasets. Existing datasets are often outdated, dominated by small or redundant graphs resulting from app repackaging, and fail to reflect the diversity of real-world malware. These limitations lead to overfitting and unreliable evaluation of graph-based classification methods. To address this gap, we introduce Better Call Graphs (BCG), a comprehensive dataset of large and unique FCGs extracted from recent Android application packages (APKs). BCG includes both benign and malicious samples spanning various families and types, along with graph-level features for each APK. Through extensive experiments using baseline classifiers, we demonstrate the necessity and value of BCG compared to existing datasets. BCG is publicly available at https://erdemub.github.io/BCG-dataset.

1bdd937594a6e58ec0ba0ab7.title_original: Clawdrain: Exploiting Tool-Calling Chains for Stealthy Token Exhaustion in OpenClaw Agents
1bdd937594a6e58ec0ba0ab7.excerpt: arXiv:2603.00902v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tool-calling LLM agents rely on third-party skills to extend their capabilities, but this openness exposes a supply-chain attack surface in which malicious skill instructions can manipulate agent execution across multiple turns. In this work, we present Clawdrain, a Trojanized OpenClaw skill that induces resource exhaustion through a Segmented Verification Process (SVP). SVP combines stateful progression, repair-driven repetition, and termination to create costly tool-calling chains while preserving a legitimate final payload. We evaluate Clawdrain in a production-like OpenClaw deployment with real API billing across Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6. Clawdrain achieves 2-16 times token amplification with plain SVP, while the three models exhibit distinct behaviors, including autoregressive compliance, proactive scripting, and extended trial-and-error reasoning. Our findings reveal that agent resource exhaustion arises not only from output generation, but also from repeated context re-ingestion, tool coordination, reasoning, and recovery, motivating system-level controls over cumulative skill behavior.

01307cd8bf95c6638b71553c.title_original: AI Agents May Always Fall for Prompt Injections
01307cd8bf95c6638b71553c.excerpt: arXiv:2605.17634v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Prompt injection is the most critical vulnerability in deployed AI agents. Despite recent progress, we show that the prevailing defense paradigm (data-instruction separation) both fails to detect attacks that operate through contextual manipulation and degrades contextually appropriate behavior. We then recast prompt injection via the lens of Contextual Integrity (CI), a privacy theory that judges information flow compliance with contextual norms. This explains types of attacks that current defenses attempt to patch and predict advanced ones future agents will face. We develop unique benign and attack scenarios that force an agent to violate the norms by (1) misrepresenting the flow, (2) manipulating norms, or (3) mixing multiple flows. This reframing suggests an impossibility argument: an adversary can always construct a context under which a blocked flow appears legitimate, or a defender who tightens norms will block genuinely legitimate flows. Our findings suggest that current research addresses a shrinking fraction of future attack surfaces. Instead, through CI, we offer a principled framework for evaluating context-sensitive failures, and designing CI-aware alignment for frontier autonomous agents.

3e356d5fb8107d7e4a2ee8a3.title_original: EduSOC: A Lightweight Simulated Security Operations Center with AI Incident Responders
3e356d5fb8107d7e4a2ee8a3.excerpt: arXiv:2605.17703v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents EduSOC, a lightweight web-based Security Operations Center (SOC) simulation platform for cybersecurity education. Conventional cyber ranges can be complex and resource-intensive to deploy, particularly for introductory exercises focused on investigative decision-making rather than infrastructure configuration. EduSOC provides an alternative by combining continuous synthetic event generation, searchable supporting evidence, and role-based artificial intelligence (AI) responders that assist investigations without revealing underlying incident classifications. Students remain responsible for interpreting evidence, consulting simulated operational teams, and justifying their escalation decisions. A preliminary classroom evaluation was conducted across three university cohorts, comprising 50 matched pre- and post-simulation survey participants. The findings indicated high student engagement and improvements in self-reported SOC self-efficacy, while short-term knowledge gains varied across cohorts. These findings provide empirical insight into the use of lightweight, AI-supported SOC simulations in university cybersecurity education.

7f4d4d9cad05b3fbbaf3045c.title_original: RAS: Measuring LLM Safety Through Refusal Alignment
7f4d4d9cad05b3fbbaf3045c.excerpt: arXiv:2606.25750v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Repeated safety evaluation of open-weight large language models requires generating and judging responses for many related checkpoints. We introduce RAS (Refusal Alignment Score), a representation-based, reference-relative indicator of harmful-request refusal computed by the five-stage SafeVec procedure. SafeVec extracts layer-wise refusal directions from an aligned reference model, measures their alignment in related targets, and calibrates a score from 0 to 100 using behavioral attack success rates (ASR) from reference and calibration models. Subsequent target scoring uses input forward passes alone. Across 18 held-out variants from the Llama, Gemma, and Qwen families, RAS correlates with $100(1-\mathrm{ASR})$ (Pearson 0.934, Spearman 0.851) and achieves 83.0% pairwise ordering agreement. Across five prompt configurations for the Llama reference, directions have mean cosine similarity 0.939. With calibration ASR already available, setup-inclusive evaluation of five targets achieves a speedup of 3.2 to 80.5 times over the specified behavioral protocol. These results support refusal alignment as an efficient signal for screening related checkpoints and prioritizing behavioral audits.

f856c928bb1fa6e8f3719650.title_original: A Re-Keying Game for Encrypted Multi-Agent Control under Persistent Threats
f856c928bb1fa6e8f3719650.excerpt: arXiv:2607.12742v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) lets a coordinator control a fleet on encrypted states, but CKKS, the approximate scheme for real-valued arithmetic, returns noisy decryptions from which an adversary can recover the secret key. Flooding each decryption with noise defends it, but a fleet must decrypt to act, so the count of decryptions grows every cycle while the loop tolerates only bounded noise. We formulate the choice of flooding and key lifetime as a leader-follower game between the fleet operator and an advanced persistent threat that listens first and then spoofs the agents' sensors. We show that the closed loop decides how long a key may be used: the formation's specification caps each key's decryption budget through the loop's $H_2$ norm, and only re-keying, not bootstrapping, renews it. A spoof consumes part of the specification that flooding needs, and the coordination graph and the cost of an alarm decide in closed form whether the scan alone, a lower flood or nothing deters it. On 196 agents escorting a convoy at 128-bit security, five graphs with the same spectral radius differ 18-fold in key lifetime, a lower flood deters the spoofer on the torus for a twentieth of a key a day, and on the ring it cuts the damage 7 times. More broadly, any system that must repeatedly decrypt to act has a key lifetime set by its tolerance to noise, making key management part of control design.

ab42752b05fe010a10cd28bf.title_original: TaintRadar: Semantic-Aware Taint-Style Vulnerability Detection via Augmented Code Property Graphs
ab42752b05fe010a10cd28bf.excerpt: arXiv:2607.16456v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite significant advances, static vulnerability analysis suffers from three critical limitations: coarse sanitization modeling (treating validation as a binary barrier), database blindness (breaking taint tracking across persistence layers), and shallow object-oriented analysis (missing field-level and interprocedural data flows). These flaws stem from a common root cause: Code Property Graph (CPG)-based taint analyses lack a compositional semantic layer to jointly model sanitization, persistence, and object aliasing. Consequently, existing tools generate excessive false positives or miss critical attack paths entirely. To address these limitations, we present TaintRadar, an approach that systematically augments CPGs with three independent semantic analysis layers. First, vulnerability-typed sanitization computes node-level safety guarantees using transfer functions and context-sensitive parameter binding. Second, persistence-aware propagation integrates database schema constraints and query safety analysis to track multi-script attack paths traversing shared database states. Finally, object-aware reaching definitions combine calling and bounded variable alias contexts to precisely model object-field mutations across method boundaries. We evaluate TaintRadar on synthetic benchmarks and real-world systems. On the SARD benchmark, TaintRadar reduces false positives while maintaining 83 percent overall accuracy. Across 19 rea

9713bfc5a0f667d0956e99a8.title_original: A Maximum Entropy Implementation of Differential Privacy Under Linear Invariants
9713bfc5a0f667d0956e99a8.excerpt: arXiv:2607.22450v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Differential privacy is the standard for ensuring data privacy and is widely used in major data publications, including reporting results from the U.S. decennial census. Common implementation of differential privacy uses independent Gaussian or Laplace noise addition to the database. However, there could be aggregate (linear) queries to the database that are excluded from the privacy budget, for example, state totals that can not be perturbed due to constitutional mandates. Any implementation of a differential privacy is required to honor these constraints, also referred to as invariants. Under aggregation constraints, the noise vector is no longer independent and the traditional differential privacy guarantees have to be re-evaluated. We propose a high entropy differential privacy implementation that maintains the aggregation invariants with probability one or exponentially close to one and derive the privacy guarantees for the implementation under the invariants. The theoretical proof also gives a solution to an open question about the null space of correlation matrices. Moreover, the methodology has general use in the context of sampling from normal mixture models under linear equality constraints.

bf3778f2a49a2a1517f1b6dc.title_original: GAZEleak: Passcode Inference Against Eye-tracking XR Devices Through External Observation
bf3778f2a49a2a1517f1b6dc.excerpt: arXiv:2609.35040v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mixed-reality headsets such as Apple Vision Pro replace the touch screen with gaze-as-pointer interaction: the wearer looks at a target and confirms with an air pinch. Because the display is inside the headset and the eye tracker is walled off from third-party software, such input is widely assumed to be unobservable to bystanders, a built-in defense against the shoulder-surfing that plagues phones and laptops. We present GAZEleak, a side-channel attack that recovers gaze-driven input from external video of head motion alone, under a strictly local, physical-observer threat model: the adversary only films the wearer from across the room and installs no software on the device. The attack exploits the centrally coupled eye-head motor program: gaze shifts recruit small, target-dependent head reorientations that project into sub-degree pose changes recoverable from commodity video. GAZEleak implements a measurement-based, sparse-optical-flow inference pipeline for users' 6-digit device passcodes. On a preliminary front-view dataset from three author-subjects who were aware of the attack hypothesis, GAZEleak places the true code within the top ten guesses for 56% (10 of 18) of test codes under a cross-person protocol with no labeled victim data, and for every code of the most exposed subject. The performance is subject-dependent: no passcode from the least exposed subject reaches the top ten, although its median guessed passcode

3c47b939bbd894fc0b84501d.title_original: A Systematic Study of Security Enforcement at Android Inter-Component Boundaries
3c47b939bbd894fc0b84501d.excerpt: arXiv:2610.13597v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Android's inter-process communication (IPC) mechanisms (Activities, Services, BroadcastReceivers, ContentProviders, and URI scheme handlers) form the primary interface between applications and between applications and the system. We present a systematic study of security enforcement comprising 120 evaluations (99 inter-component interface evaluations across five interface categories, 10 platform security-control evaluations, and 11 dedicated positive controls) in over 30 Google and AOSP packages on Android 17 (API 37). Using an expected-versus-observed framework under a zero-permission attacker model, we evaluate whether each boundary's enforcement mechanism functions as designed. We find 97 enforcement gaps (80.8%) and 23 enforcement holds (19.2%). From these observations, we derive a 14-category enforcement gap taxonomy organized across manifest, code, platform, and architectural layers. Within our purposively selected corpus, observed enforcement outcomes differ substantially across interface categories: evaluated Activities and BroadcastReceivers exhibit a 100% gap rate, while ContentProviders, which benefit from framework-provided defenses such as setStrict(), achieve a 27.6% holds rate. We find that all seven evaluated platform compatibility changes with security intent are either disabled or gated at a targetSdkVersion that none of the applications in our evaluated corpus targets. We document 18 custom URI scheme regi

889b64ecc67b60d45fe4a4de.title_original: AI Security Literacy: Ecosystem-Based Competency Framework and K-12 Learning Platform
889b64ecc67b60d45fe4a4de.excerpt: arXiv:2610.28859v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Adoption of artificial intelligence in K-12 schools has outpaced guidance for students, teachers, and administrators. Existing AI-literacy frameworks emphasize understanding and use; cybersecurity frameworks predate AI-specific threats, and neither defines AI security literacy as a competency domain in its own right. We propose an AI Security Literacy (AISL) framework of six dimensions spanning the school ecosystem, ground its technical dimensions in public AI-safety benchmarks and a reproducible multi-seed adversarial evaluation, and ground its attitudinal dimensions in nationally representative survey micro-data from U.S. teachers and adults. Only 34.5% of teachers report a school AI policy, and teachers see their own AI use as easing their work but students' use as complicating it; on the technical side, a reported robustness figure depends as much on the attack and the particular trained model as on the system evaluated. NeuralFortify, a browser-based K-12 platform built on real AI models, is presented as an illustrative operationalization.

ea07cf556c510d23790c5c58.title_original: Reconstructing False Alarm and Detection Rates in Quantum Machine Learning for Intrusion Detection
ea07cf556c510d23790c5c58.excerpt: arXiv:2610.35235v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Published results in quantum machine learning for intrusion detection (QML-IDS) require joint interpretation of false-positive rate (FPR), attack true-positive rate (TPR), and evaluation provenance. We reconstruct operating points in the 25-entry frame selected by Kaissar and colleagues: 21 included articles, 20 identified documentary families, substantive methodological material consulted for 15, and 24 descriptive points from five. In one test-labelled comparison, a quantum support vector machine reduces FPR from 6.875% for random forest to 3.329%, while TPR decreases from 93.955% to 93.682%; both rates improve against three other comparators. In another study, a complete benign row identifies FPR as 12/6000 (0.200%), despite incomplete attack-side allocation that requires additional assumptions for TPR. Normalized matrices identify detection ranges rather than a unique aggregate rate. A uniform provenance rule separates training-described and test-adjusted results from six conditional illustrations whose independence remains unverified. The contribution is a reproducible interpretation of favorable comparisons and detection trade-offs, without converting descriptive results or hypothetical calculations into operational guarantees.

f7320f8621527a3c730a5a3a.title_original: Fooling Relying Parties of the EUDI Wallet Architecture: Credential Pooling Attacks and CRESTA, a Standard-Compliant Countermeasure
f7320f8621527a3c730a5a3a.excerpt: arXiv:2610.41655v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The European Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet will let millions of EU citizens prove who they are and what they are entitled to, disclosing only what is needed. Many services need several credentials at once, such as an identity card and a university degree, so combined presentations are essential. We present credential pooling attacks on relying parties of the EUDI Wallet reference architecture. Colluding users, each holding some credentials in their own wallet, cooperate through a proxy that acts as a single synthetic user and presents all the requested credentials, although no single user holds them all. Every signature is genuine and computed by certified hardware, and nothing is extracted or forged. We ran the attack against the European Commission's reference implementation, also on two Android phones. The attack would fail if all credentials of a user carried the same public key, but colluding relying parties could then link all presentations of that user. For this reason, the Architecture and Reference Framework (ARF) requires a fresh key for each credential and recommends batches of single-use copies, each with its own key: precisely what makes pooling possible. One might think that preventing pooling requires giving up unlinkability or adopting non-standard cryptography, such as zero-knowledge proofs. 30105c2655f03adbfe7be9c9.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12807v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is widely used to customize large language models, but third-party adapters create supply-chain backdoor risks with under 1% modified parameters. Recent analytical null-space and subspace projection defenses report near-zero static Attack Success Rates (ASR), equating static silence with erasure. We audit subspace-projection defenses across four scales (Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B), three architectures (Qwen2.5, InternLM2.5-1.8B, Spark-X2.6-4B), and five trigger families (suffix, natural phrase, prefix/in-sentence, double-negation syntax, and composite triggers). Statically, module-wise rank-1 trigger-difference projection cuts ASR from 60.4% to 0.0% on standard suites and 70.3% to 0.0% on 1,000 uncontaminated prompts (p = 3.055e-299) in under 5 s. By Theorem 1 (11,880/11,880 module-sample pairs), low-rank bottleneck amplification aligns benign polite-suffix probes with u_1(B) (median cosine 0.8934-0.9705), reaching 0.0% ASR without trigger knowledge. However, static suppression is not erasure. Under 5-sample reactivation, single-round weight-editing baselines rebound to 91.7%-100.0% ASR in Epoch 1 (Fine-Pruning, ANP, NEEDLE, LoRA-Patch; 48.7% for single-round dual projection) and 100.0% by Epoch 2. Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 prove single-sided projection leaves non-zero gradients along u_1 across 168/168 modules (27.2x-31.1x above random expectation), while Haar orthogonal rotation shows Epoch-2 immuni

2f65ce45b48d35d870eae8b1.title_original: EDGChain-E: A Decentralized Git-Based Framework for Versioning Encrypted Energy Data
2f65ce45b48d35d870eae8b1.excerpt: arXiv:2507.01615v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper proposes a new decentralized framework, named EDGChain-E (Encrypted-Data-Git Chain for Energy), designed to manage version-controlled, encrypted energy data using blockchain and the InterPlanetary File System. The framework incorporates a Decentralized Autonomous Organization (DAO) to orchestrate collaborative data governance across the lifecycle of energy research and operations, such as smart grid monitoring, demand forecasting, and peer-to-peer energy trading. In EDGChain-E, initial commits capture the full encrypted datasets-such as smart meter readings or grid telemetry-while subsequent updates are tracked as encrypted Git patches, ensuring integrity, traceability, and privacy. This versioning mechanism supports secure collaboration across multiple stakeholders (e.g., utilities, researchers, regulators) without compromising sensitive or regulated information. We highlight the framework's capability to maintain FAIR-compliant (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) provenance of encrypted data. By embedding hash-based content identifiers in Merkle trees, the system enables transparent, auditable, and immutable tracking of data changes, thereby supporting reproducibility and trust in decentralized energy applications.

8be5824412ae0e206d972e68.title_original: NL-SME: Enhancing Multi-Step Gradient Inversion through Adaptive Two-State Matching
8be5824412ae0e206d972e68.excerpt: arXiv:2509.22082v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training among multiple clients without directly sharing their raw data.However, gradient inversion attacks can exploit the model updates exchanged during training to reconstruct clients' private data.With multiple local training steps, an observed update combines gradients evaluated at changing model states and potentially different mini-batches, while intermediate states remain hidden. Restricting gradient evaluation to a single state on the segment between the initial and final models can exclude states that better fit the accumulated update.We consider reconstruction from an individual client's endpoint models, assuming that the training labels are known.We propose NL-SME, a regularized two-state gradient surrogate for matching multi-step client updates without replaying local training.The surrogate adapts its evaluation center, regularizes its displacement, and averages raw parameter gradients at two shared symmetric states.We evaluate NL-SME against existing gradient inversion methods on FEMNIST and CIFAR-100 with varying numbers of local training steps.The results show improved reconstruction quality, highlighting the privacy risks of sharing individual client updates after multiple local steps.

96e87771de41514c418fb075.title_original: On the Price of Privacy for Language Identification and Generation
96e87771de41514c418fb075.excerpt: arXiv:2604.07238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models train on sensitive user data, so we ask what differential privacy (DP) costs in language learning. We study private language identification and generation in the agnostic statistical setting. For identification, privacy is free: at every fixed $\varepsilon$, pure DP and $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP with $\delta\ge n^{-O(1)}$ keep the non-private rate $\exp(-r(n))$ for every $r(n)=o(n)$. For generation, the price depends on what is public. With a public witness bound, pure DP loses at most a factor $\Theta(\min\{1,\varepsilon\})$ in the exponent, and on suitable two-language collections the optimal rate is $\exp(-\Theta(\min\{1,\varepsilon\}\,n))$. Without such a bound, pure DP can lose the exponential rate itself, already for two languages: every rate $\exp(-o(n))$ stays achievable, but no exponential rate is. On these collections, $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP keeps an exponential rate if and only if $\log(1/\delta)=o(n)$. Three facts about pure DP drive the proofs. It turns a robustness margin into an exponentially small error. It obeys a private form of Le Cam's two-point bound. And it cannot see the absence of a string.

d6967a318368eb6520cf8dba.title_original: Not What a Child Expressed: Auditing the Sign-to-Text Safety Interface in Child-Facing AI
d6967a318368eb6520cf8dba.excerpt: arXiv:2610.07519v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Automatic sign language translation (SLT) has entered consumer products, turning American Sign Language into English text for dictation, messaging, and queries put to a conversational assistant. Child-facing AI and platform trust-and-safety tooling decide on text, using filters on minor accounts and grooming classifiers that score chat messages. A signing child who uses SLT therefore reaches these safeguards through a translation. We found no publicly documented system in which the two have been jointly evaluated, and the leading deployed SLT model was neither trained nor formally evaluated on signers under 18. Errors that alter negation, participant roles, secrecy, urgency or help-seeking could change a safety decision without disturbing fluency. This paper proposes a Deaf-informed pre-deployment audit of that boundary, with a failure taxonomy, a sanitised scenario schema, four comparison conditions, and four outcome measures. Auslan is the planned first case study.

def05c6921270af4a276cfd7.title_original: High-Throughput Private Information Retrieval with on-CPU Accelerators
def05c6921270af4a276cfd7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.02376v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present AltoPIR, the first PIR system that exploits the capability of emerging on-CPU matrix accelerators such as Intel AMX. Unlike existing solutions, AltoPIR achieves high-performance PIR through efficient batching without requiring discrete accelerators. However, the on-CPU accelerator has only a few small registers and shares its core with request handling. As a result, it runs far below its peak rate while its operands arrive from memory, and it remains idle while its core handles requests. To keep the accelerator busy, we design mechanisms that reduce both the memory traffic of a batch and the core cycles spent on each request. Our experimental results show that AltoPIR outperforms existing CPU-based solutions by up to 50.1x.

89051e31262106d745ef3ba4.background_ko: Microsoft 365 로그인 토큰을 탈취해 재사용하면 다중요소 인증을 마친 세션과 클라우드 자원에 접근할 수 있다는 점이 공격에 악용된다.

curation.reason_ko: 다중요소 인증 이후의 Microsoft 365 세션을 노리는 피싱 키트 분석으로 토큰 기반 침해 대응에 유용하다.

13e711f6631054c9334ad4b5.title_original: Microsoft testing Remote Lock for lost or stolen Windows devices
13e711f6631054c9334ad4b5.excerpt: Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets enterprise IT administrators remotely lock stolen or lost Windows devices without wiping them. [...]
13e711f6631054c9334ad4b5.title_ko: Microsoft, 분실·도난 Windows 기기용 원격 잠금 기능 시험
13e711f6631054c9334ad4b5.summary_ko: Microsoft가 Windows 11 Insider Preview에서 기업 관리자가 Intune으로 기기를 원격 잠그는 Remote Lock을 시험하고 있다. 데이터를 삭제하지 않고 모든 활성 세션과 로그인 수단을 차단하며, 재시작하거나 오프라인 상태여도 잠금이 유지된다. 다만 네트워크 격리나 외부 매체 부팅 차단 기능은 아니다.
13e711f6631054c9334ad4b5.background_ko: 기업 IT 관리자가 분실·도난된 Windows 기기를 초기화하지 않고 원격으로 잠글 수 있도록 마련한 기능이다.

curation.reason_ko: 데이터 삭제 없이 분실 Windows 기기를 잠그는 기능을 시험해 기업 단말 분실 대응에 참고가 된다.

6d2c50856efd9c14f74422d9.title_original: AI Framework Autonomously Weaponized Flaws in Real Attacks, Google Says
6d2c50856efd9c14f74422d9.excerpt: Threat actors are deploying multi-agent offensive frameworks to increase the velocity of multi-stage intrusions. The post AI Framework Autonomously Weaponized Flaws in Real Attacks, Google Says appeared first on SecurityWeek .
6d2c50856efd9c14f74422d9.title_ko: Google, 실제 공격에서 취약점 탐지·악용 자동화한 AI 프레임워크 발견
6d2c50856efd9c14f74422d9.summary_ko: Google GTIG는 공격자가 사람의 개입 없이 취약점 탐지와 악용을 자동화하는 AI 프레임워크를 사용한 사례를 확인했다고 밝혔다. 노출된 준비 서버에서 발견한 exploit_agent는 패치 전후 코드를 비교해 공격 코드를 만들고 실행하도록 설계됐다. 서버에서는 피해자에게서 탈취한 데이터와 침투 후 활동용 스크립트도 발견됐다.
6d2c50856efd9c14f74422d9.background_ko: GTIG는 공격자들이 패치 분석과 알려진 취약점의 무기화를 가속하고 공격 규모를 늘리기 위해 LLM과 다중 에이전트 프레임워크를 도입하고 있다고 설명했다.

curation.reason_ko: Google이 공격자 서버에서 패치 분석과 공격 코드 생성을 자동화하는 AI 도구를 발견했다고 밝혔다.

02b4c834b628d81d371954d3.summary_ko: Ipsos가 내부 정보시스템 한 곳에서 발생한 침해 사고를 조사하고 있으며, 외부 보안 전문가와 함께 대응·차단 조치를 진행했다고 밝혔다. 회사는 업무와 고객 서비스에 영향이 없었다고 설명했지만, 데이터 접근·유출 여부와 침투 경로, 구체적인 피해 범위는 아직 공개하지 않았다.

1242b5f16d5314cf6a2f4ce6.title_original: Fandango Warns Ticket Buyers of Payment Card Data Exposure
1242b5f16d5314cf6a2f4ce6.excerpt: Card numbers, CVVs, expiration dates, and email addresses used at Fandango’s ticketing checkout over four days in October may have been exposed. The post Fandango Warns Ticket Buyers of Payment Card Data Exposure appeared first on SecurityWeek .
1242b5f16d5314cf6a2f4ce6.title_ko: Fandango, 일부 영화표 구매 고객의 결제카드 정보 노출 가능성 통지
1242b5f16d5314cf6a2f4ce6.summary_ko: Fandango가 2026년 10월 8~11일 결제 페이지에서 이뤄진 일부 거래의 카드 정보에 비인가자가 접근했을 가능성을 고객에게 알렸다. 노출 가능 정보는 카드번호·CVV·유효기간·청구지 우편번호와 이메일 주소이며, 회사는 문제를 해결했고 관련 부정 사용은 아직 파악되지 않았다고 밝혔다. 침입 경위와 전체 영향 인원은 공개하지 않았다.

curation.reason_ko: Fandango가 카드번호·CVV 등 노출 가능성을 통지했으며 전체 규모와 부정 사용 여부는 미확인이다.

a2b9d03f283caf325384137f.title_original: Pretxt Emerges Stealth With $5M Seed and an AI Supervision Tool
a2b9d03f283caf325384137f.excerpt: Pretxt provides technology to prevent AI agents escaping their guardrails and causing unintended harm. The post Pretxt Emerges Stealth With $5M Seed and an AI Supervision Tool appeared first on SecurityWeek .
a2b9d03f283caf325384137f.title_ko: Pretxt, 500만 달러 시드 투자 유치…AI 에이전트 실시간 감독 도구 공개
a2b9d03f283caf325384137f.summary_ko: Pretxt가 500만 달러의 시드 투자를 유치하고 AI 에이전트의 행동을 실행 중 감독하는 ‘AI Supervision’을 공개했다. 회사는 에이전트의 지시와 권한, 고객이 정한 제한을 바탕으로 상호작용을 점검하며, 문제가 감지되면 작동을 중단하기보다 허용된 업무로 되돌리도록 유도한다고 설명했다.
a2b9d03f283caf325384137f.background_ko: AI 에이전트가 모호한 지시를 잘못 해석해 의도하지 않은 행동을 할 위험에 대응하면서도 업무 수행 능력을 과도하게 제한하지 않으려는 취지다.

189bd7807378e3b58c18b14b.title_original: MSP ScreenConnect Servers Targeted in Month-Long Campaign
189bd7807378e3b58c18b14b.excerpt: More than 40 servers received over 688,000 requests exploiting CVE-2026-84869 to execute guest-pushed files. The post MSP ScreenConnect Servers Targeted in Month-Long Campaign appeared first on SecurityWeek .
189bd7807378e3b58c18b14b.title_ko: MSP ScreenConnect 서버 42곳 겨냥한 공격…패치된 취약점 악용
189bd7807378e3b58c18b14b.summary_ko: Huntress는 9월 패치된 CVE-2026-84869를 악용해 MSP의 ScreenConnect 서버 42곳에 악성 파일 실행 요청이 최소 68만8천 건 전송됐다고 밝혔다. 기술자가 원격 세션에 접속하면 확인창 없이 파일이 실행되며, 악성 ScreenConnect 클라이언트를 설치한 사례가 관찰됐다. 기사에서는 기술자용 호스트 클라이언트를 26.6.5 이상으로, 관련 Access 에이전트도 업데이트하도록 권고했다.
189bd7807378e3b58c18b14b.background_ko: 인증·권한 관리 결함으로 원격 세션에서 승인이나 확인 없이 파일을 전송·실행할 수 있어, 공격자가 기술자의 세션 참여를 노려 악성 파일을 실행했다.

curation.reason_ko: MSP 서버 42곳에 대한 악용 요청과 악성 클라이언트 설치가 관찰돼 원격관리 환경 대응이 시급하다.

6da68c1bb4e81d3f831ae0c0.excerpt: Hackers breached Access Dental’s network and stole personal, health, and insurance information. The post Access Dental Management Data Breach Impacts Over 340,000 appeared first on SecurityWeek .
6da68c1bb4e81d3f831ae0c0.title_ko: 미국 Access Dental Management 개인정보 유출…34만여 명 피해 신고

curation.reason_ko: 34만여 명의 의료·보험 정보 등이 침해됐다고 신고돼 민감정보를 다루는 의료 서비스 보안에 중요하다.

4b747d5ae931d2f81684bdef.excerpt: Led by NEA and supported by existing investors, the funding brings the company’s valuation to $1 billion. The post Corma Receives $125 Million to Train Foundation Models for Defensive Cybersecurity appeared first on SecurityWeek .

5c98fd91975647da1f7c77d1.title_original: N-able Kills Legacy APIs, Patches 17 N-central Zero-Days

09a2ca5ec574bc77f2190a31.title_original: Security for the agentic era, powered by Microsoft Perception
09a2ca5ec574bc77f2190a31.excerpt: In this article A new cyber stack, built to fight AI with AI Delivering agentic security at Microsoft Ignite Secure your foundations Defend with agents Secure agentic insiders Changing how security work gets done Explore what's new A year ago, finding a serious, exploitable vulnerability was slow and expensive work done by elite security researchers. That’s no longer true. Over the past 12 months, frontier AI models have become remarkably good at discovering and exploiting software vulnerabilities, and similar levels of capability are quickly becoming available in open weights models with limited cyber guardrails. Attacks that once required specialized resources are now within reach of almost anyone. We saw what that looks like in a single week this fall when PHP disclosed two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities, flaws that let an attacker take control of a server with a single request over the internet. 1 At the time of disclosure, tens of millions of internet-facing PHP services were running affected versions. Nearly two weeks later, about 29 million services remained vulnerable. Behind those servers are banks, healthcare providers, energy companies, and much of the infrastructure the internet runs on. And that same day brought five other major disclosures across the industry. 09a2ca5ec574bc77f2190a31.summary_ko: Microsoft가 보안 에이전트 조율 플랫폼 Perception의 정식 출시를 발표했다. 공격을 모의하는 레드팀, 위협을 탐지·조사하는 블루팀, 문제를 수정하는 그린팀 에이전트를 연계하며, 보안팀이 통제 기준을 정하고 영향이 큰 조치를 승인하도록 설계됐다.

curation.reason_ko: Microsoft가 공격 모의·탐지·수정 에이전트를 조율하는 Perception 정식 출시와 승인 구조를 발표했다.

71853ef952e2bfb0eef37813.title_original: The risks of device code authentication for AI coding agents
71853ef952e2bfb0eef37813.excerpt: In this article From a familiar phishing technique to an AI coding agent How the attack works One approval, four ways the impact can spread Turning a phishing attempt into a Defender signal Mitigation and protection guidance References Learn More Device code phishing has become a recurring route to account takeover. Instead of stealing a password, an attacker persuades someone to approve a sign-in on a legitimate site simply by entering a code. The resulting access often can reach email, files, or other cloud services, depending on the account and the permissions granted. Notable earlier campaigns such as EvilTokens show how readily this technique can be scaled to do real damage. Microsoft worked hard with partners in industry and law enforcement to disrupt EvilTokens in September 2026. That led us to a different question: what else can an attacker do with a phished device code authorization? What happens when the same trick targets an AI agent rather than a mailbox? We used GitHub Copilot CLI as an illustrative example. Depending on its configuration, it can work with code, run commands on a user’s machine, retain context across sessions, and allow an active session to be steered remotely. 2ed81c562618ef5d63e206f6.title_original: PAC Reasoning: Controlling the Performance Loss for Efficient Reasoning
2ed81c562618ef5d63e206f6.excerpt: arXiv:2510.09133v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) have achieved remarkable progress in complex problem-solving tasks. Despite this success, LRMs typically suffer from high computational costs during deployment, highlighting a need for efficient inference. A practical direction is to switch the LRM between thinking and non-thinking modes dynamically. However, such approaches often introduce additional reasoning errors and lack statistical guarantees for the performance loss, which are critical for high-stakes applications. In this work, we propose Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) Reasoning that controls the performance loss under the user-specified tolerance. Specifically, we construct an upper confidence bound on the performance loss and determine a threshold for switching to the non-thinking model. Theoretically, using the threshold to switch between the thinking and non-thinking modes ensures bounded performance loss in a distribution-free manner. Our experiments on reasoning benchmarks show that the proposed method can save computational budgets and control the user-specified performance loss.

596312119ac1464554e82285.title_original: GenPFN: An In-Context Tabular Foundation Model Approach for Augmenting Small Datasets in Engineering
596312119ac1464554e82285.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14804v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Costly simulations and experiments limit the data available for engineering design. This paper proposes GenPFN, a training-free candidate generator guided by a pretrained tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) classifier with fixed weights. The context contains evaluated designs labeled desired (Class 1) or undesired (Class 0). GenPFN interpolates between desired designs and refines candidates using gated classifier gradients and Gaussian noise. Each candidate is evaluated using the problem's constraints and objective functions. Evaluated desired designs and their objective values augment the context for regression training. Evaluation spans fourteen selected problems, including a two-parameter benchmark and a 44-parameter hull problem. In paired comparisons, GenPFN with TabPFN v1 achieves higher class satisfaction and lower realism distance than the tested adversarial, variational-autoencoder and diffusion generators. The variational-autoencoder generator provides greater coverage and diversity. Relative to the synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE), GenPFN provides lower coverage distance and greater diversity. Among observed paired regression fits, augmentation reduces estimated AutoGluon validation mean squared error by 62.1% relative to context-only training. 4ce6bb44c1571ab30124b140.title_original: Early Signals, Strong Decisions: Prefix-Guided Sampling for Parallel Test-Time Scaling
4ce6bb44c1571ab30124b140.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14965v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parallel test-time scaling (TTS) has been shown to enhance reasoning in large language models by generating and aggregating multiple independent reasoning paths. Internal confidence scores can further improve this process by identifying paths of varying quality. However, existing methods remain computationally inefficient, as low-quality paths are fully expanded before being evaluated. In this work, we aim to improve the use of internal confidence signals for better model performance and computational efficiency. We begin by offering a new perspective on the role of confidence in aggregation, showing that it is most impactful for questions near the decision boundary. Notably, when amplified by multi-sample aggregation, even small confidence signals derived from short prefixes can meaningfully influence outcomes in these boundary cases. Building on this insight, we introduce Prefix-Guided Sampling (PreG), a method that reallocates computation by first generating short prefixes, ranking them using internal confidence scores, and then completing only the most promising candidates. This strategy reduces token usage while maintaining gains in path quality. We provide theoretical analysis demonstrating that, under a fixed compute budget, PreG strengthens the effective signal by widening the decision boundary margin. Empirically, our method consistently outperforms standard parallel TTS approaches across benchmarks, while significa

5a551c2ac063a5fbcc76a76a.title_original: Can MLLMs Reason over Surround-View Driving Videos? A Multi-View Autonomous Driving QA Benchmark
5a551c2ac063a5fbcc76a76a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.15225v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Surround-view video understanding in autonomous driving is a crucial capability for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to achieve reliable driving reasoning. Real-world driving often requires information beyond the front-view camera. Existing MLLMs primarily focus on front-view information, while their spatio-temporal understanding and reasoning abilities remain unknown. To address this gap, we propose MVDriveBench, a high-information-density video QA benchmark for autonomous driving, characterized by synchronized surround-view inputs, spatio-temporal understanding, and reasoning-chain-oriented evaluation. We design 12 categories of QA tasks that cover the complete reasoning pipeline from low-level visual perception to high-level driving decision-making, enabling a systematic evaluation of MLLMs surround-view spatio-temporal understanding and reasoning capabilities in complex driving environments. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of 23 open-source, closed-source, and expert MLLMs on MVDriveBench. The results show that current MLLMs still exhibit insufficient surround-view spatio-temporal reasoning ability. Meanwhile, closed-loop evaluations of specialist models in AlpaSim reveal a correlation between surround-view spatio-temporal reasoning capabilities and closed-loop driving performance, highlighting the importance of comprehensive multi-view understanding for reliable vehicle control.

e159875ec975bd175dfe76ca.title_original: Small Heads, Strong Decisions: A Controlled Study of Typed-Decision Models
e159875ec975bd175dfe76ca.excerpt: arXiv:2611.15592v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In September 2026, TypeSafe announced Jev as the first model in its System One category: unstructured state goes in, and typed, calibrated decisions that software can use directly come out. They answer structured questions about a piece of text, such as a yes/no check, a choice among labelled options or a graded score, by reading the text with a language model and scoring the options with a small readout. Each pairs a different readout with a different backbone, training mix and recipe, so it is unclear which design choices matter. We re-implement five readouts and train all of them under one protocol: the same backbone, the same 15 public English training sources, the same recipe with a per-head learning-rate sweep, and the same seed. Reading all of a text's questions from one prompt also matches one prompt per question in accuracy, with 1.6 times faster inference and 2.1-2.5 times faster training on one H100. The bac

1bb96bee05749745c662650b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.16493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As agents perform tasks autonomously in local and cloud environments, auditing their execution trajectories can help service providers identify risks and improve agent harnesses and foundation models. Our analysis of production and red-team trajectories shows that some risks are repeatedly missed across auditing configurations. Overall recall obscures which risks are missed and whether higher recall comes with more false positives on legitimate behavior. Existing benchmarks offer limited insight into these failures. Generated trajectories can contain inconsistent tool calls and responses, conspicuous risky actions, or repetitive attack patterns. Grouping results by risk type also makes it difficult to tell whether auditors overlooked evidence, accepted an unsupported conclusion, or lacked information needed to make a judgment. We introduce ReA-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark for auditing responsible agent behavior. It organizes auditing challenges into six tiers: internal safety knowledge, contradictions within trajectories, evidence retrieval in long contexts, verification of sources and reasoning, indirect steering, and missing information. It includes challenging benign cases in which actions resemble risky ones but are consistent with the task and its authorization. Yet existing benchmarks often restrict agents to narrow action spaces, use simplified environments, or rely on verification methods that are unreliable for evaluating arbitrary agent-generated systems. Additionally, through extensive red-teaming covering 9 of the 10 categories in the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, we expose reward-hacking vulnerabilities in the conventional Harbor framework and develop Breakwater, an extension of Harbor that blocks all attacks tested in our study. Across 11 agents built from 7 frontier models and 2 harnesses, Opus 5.5 with Claude Code matches or outperforms the human baseline on all six tasks with a Singularity-Index of 1.25, suggesting it may have the skills needed to reach the singularity. 56bf3ab9d7b10453a9687590.title_original: InertiaMPDD: Multimodal Personalized Depression Detection via Emotional Inertia-Inspired Dynamics Modeling
56bf3ab9d7b10453a9687590.excerpt: arXiv:2611.16647v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multimodal depression screening estimates risk from speech, visual behavior and language. Current methods mainly predict labels, with limited evidence of departures from a non-depressed reference. Recording-level supervision also leaves fine-grained emotional dynamics unannotated. Motivated by emotional inertia, the persistence of affect, InertiaMPDD learns healthy next-state patterns using a world-model-inspired latent predictor. Using pretrained multimodal representations, it predicts from observed history and context. Reference deviation, residual decay rate and a Jacobian spectral descriptor form reference-derived emotional dynamics descriptors, evaluated as candidate proxy biomarkers for standalone screening and personalized decision correction. Across five cohorts from four datasets, fusion reaches 98.41% F1 on D-Vlog and 84.98% on LMVD. Standalone descriptors outperform fixed additive fusion on MPDD but discriminate weakly on AVEC2014. These findings distinguish reference informativeness from fusion benefit and reveal context-dependent utility.

ce896473fc7e7cbd6c48d4d9.title_original: Skill Adapter: Personalized Modification and Online Routing of General-Purpose Skills
ce896473fc7e7cbd6c48d4d9.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17007v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents use external skills to reuse task procedures and experience with tools. General-purpose skills describe shared execution procedures, while specific tool choices, operating practices, and output requirements vary across users. In long-horizon tasks, subgoals, available inputs, and environmental states change as execution progresses. Agents must select currently applicable skills from an expanding skill pool and prepare candidates for subsequent steps. We propose Skill Adapter, which enables personalized modification and online routing of general-purpose skills. The system distills local adjustments from user requirements and execution feedback and stores them as Adapters linked to general-purpose skills. The routing agent selects general-purpose skills and applicable Adapters based on the current subtask, execution progress, and environmental feedback, incrementally maintaining a task-level online skill library that the main LLM reads on demand. The system preloads candidates for subsequent nodes and rechecks their applicability once actual inputs are determined. Reinforcement learning optimizes the two types of decisions using modification gains and routing outcomes, respectively. We evaluate Skill Adapter on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SkillsBench. Compared with SkillRL, it improves task success rates by an average of 11.43 percentage points and reduces mean execution time on all three benchmark

661f75771044a64c87ff4dbe.excerpt: arXiv:2601.16809v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: AI coding agents such as GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex and Devin now open pull requests (PRs) that are merged into open-source projects. 1d0ceb3455c6b04fa7402311.title_original: Reframing Video Inverse Tone Mapping as Blind Posterior Inference via Latent Luminance Supervision
1d0ceb3455c6b04fa7402311.excerpt: arXiv:2611.15146v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: High-dynamic-range (HDR) displays are now common, but most video content, such as archival footage, broadcast material, and the output of generative video models, exists only in standard dynamic range (SDR). The need is sharpest for generated video, which has no HDR master at all and is graded alongside live-action and visual-effects material finished in HDR. Converting SDR to HDR means undoing a tone-mapping operation that was never recorded, and clipping destroys the radiance wherever it acts, so HDR recovery is a blind inverse problem. Methods built on generative video priors fill clipped regions with plausible structure, but their reconstructions are systematically biased: in every public method we test, saturated content leans too bright or too dark, and the direction of the lean moves with the tone operator behind the input. We call this failure the luminance error, measure both its magnitude and its sign, and make it the focus of this work. Reframing ITM as posterior inference under an unknown operator locates the failure in two places and yields two corrections. A fixed affine functional of the video-diffusion latent reads log-luminance without decoding; on that coordinate an asymmetric loss selects an expectile of the posterior, applied only where clipping leaves luminance unconstrained. b436a01fa047764b5b750296.title_original: Runtime Analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming on Max: A Proven Exponential Speedup
b436a01fa047764b5b750296.excerpt: arXiv:2611.16013v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Genetic Programming (GP) is a search paradigm inspired from natural evolution for the automated discovery of expressions, functions, and computer programs. Cartesian GP (CGP) is a flavor of GP that uses a graph-based model to encode candidate programs, as contrasted to the conventional Tree-based GP (TGP). Since its inception two decades ago, CGP has predominantly been analyzed empirically, thus little is known regarding its theoretical performance guarantees. This paper analyzes CGP for the Max problem, which has been only rigorously studied for TGP with a proven expected runtime superlinear in the optimal program length $n$. We prove that the expected time for the ($1$+$1$) CGP employing common mutation operators to evolve an equivalent optimal of the same output is polylogarithmic in $n$, specifically at most $O(\log^9{n})$. This is remarkable, as it shows an exponential speedup by switching to CGP. Our results shed light on the benefit and the compactness of the graph-based representation for programs, and on how CGP can navigate its search and fitness spaces efficiently. This is a first proven performance guarantee for CGP on an established benchmark problem. Experiments complement our theoretical findings.

6faaebc150f7cb1d36f93588.title_original: Pyramidal Columns Acting as Attention Heads
6faaebc150f7cb1d36f93588.excerpt: arXiv:2611.16057v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Can the functional architecture of a Transformer attention head be given a biological construction? More specifically, could a suitable group of pyramidal columns in posterior temporal language regions (PTLRs) constitute the biological construction of a neuromorphic mechanical realization of an attention head, under a mathematical instantiation that need not coincide with its standard Transformer instantiation? c6d97c03dd402eb660c3e76d.title_original: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
c6d97c03dd402eb660c3e76d.excerpt: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely , a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC , CNN , Equifax , Ledger and Zoom , was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content. The Zoom.com homepage loading the malicious JavaScript file from Optimizely. Image: blog.report-uri.com. Click to enlarge. According to a blog post from the security firm Report URI , on November 16 malicious JavaScript code was served to visitors of 178 organizations through Optimizely’s platform. Report URI researcher Scott Helme wrote that the payload delivered by the malicious Javascript was rebuilt 26 times during the day, dropping a multi-purpose malware kit that could steal payment card data, cookies and screenshots, and swap any cryptocurrency payment addresses for the attacker’s. Helme noted the affected websites also served exploit code custom made to attack known vulnerabilities in older Apple iPhone and iPad devices. 93243ae5929fdfb9c7d9c5fb.title_original: 자바(Java), 인증 없이 원격 코드 실행 가능한 ‘Java4Shell’ 취약점(CVE-2026-114938) 긴급 업데이트 권고
93243ae5929fdfb9c7d9c5fb.excerpt: 생성형 AI 제작 이미지 오라클(Oracle)과 OpenJDK가 자바(Java) 실행 환경에서 발견된 원격 코드 실행 취약점(CVE-2026-114938, 일명 Java4Shell)에 대한 보안 업데이트를 배포했습니다. 이번 취약점은 자바 가상 머신(JVM)인 HotSpot이 Base64 디코딩을 빠르게 처리하기 위해 사용하는 하드웨어 가속 코드에서 발생하는 '힙 메모리 경계 밖 쓰기(Out-of-Bounds Write)' 결함입니다. AVX-512 명령어를 지원하는 x86-64 서버에서 끝부분에 패딩 문자('=')가 붙은 조작된 Base64 문자열을 디코딩할 때, 출력 길이가 음수로 잘못 계산되면서 결과를 저장하는 배열의 범위를 넘어 메모리를 덮어쓰게 됩니다. Base64 디코딩은 로그인 인증, 파일 업로드 등 웹 서비스의 일반적인 기능에서 폭넓게 사용되기 때문에, 공격자는 인증 없이 원격에서 조작된 요청을 보내는 것만으로 서버의 메모리를 손상시키고 임의 코드를 실행할 수 있습니다. 국가사이버안보센터도 세부 내용 공개에 앞서 보안 권고를 발표한 만큼 자바를 사용하는 서버 운영자분들의 신속한 업데이트를 권고 드립니다. 취약점 개요 CVE CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell) 영향 컴포넌트 OpenJDK HotSpot 컴파일러(hotspot/compiler) x86-64용 Base64 디코딩 인트린직(AVX-512 VBMI 가속 코드), java.util.Base64 기본/URL 디코더 취약점 유형 정수 언더플로로 인한 힙 메모리 경계 밖 쓰기(Out-of-Bounds Write) 인증 없이 원격에서 메모리 손상, 정보 유출 및 임의 코드 실행 가능 심각도 High (CVSS v3.1 8.1) 영향 대상 OpenJDK 17.0.6 이상 및 이를 기반으로 한 자바 17/21/25/27 배포판 AVX-512 VBMI를 지원하는 x86-64 CPU에서 실행되는 경우에 한함 (ARM64 해당 없음) 실제 악용 실제 공격에 악용된 사례는 보고되지 않음 (2026. 11. 18. 기준) 발견자가 취약점 재현 코드를 공개했으며, 제품별 공격 코드는 비공개 조치 Oracle Java SE 및 OpenJDK 배포판의 11월 보안 업데이트 적용 후 자바 애플리케이션 재시작 취약점 발생 원인 자바의 JIT 컴파일러는 자주 실행되는 표준 라이브러리 기능 일부를 CPU에 최적화된 어셈블리 코드로 바꿔 실행하는데, 이를 인트린직(Intrinsic)이라고 합니다. java.util.Base64 의 디코딩 기능도 그중 하나로, OpenJDK 17.0.6부터 AVX-512 명령어를 지원하는 x86-64 CPU에서는 64바이트 단위로 데이터를 한 번에 처리하는 가속 코드가 사용됩니다. 문제는 이 가속 코드가 입력의 마지막 부분을 처리하는 방식에 있습니다. 가속 코드는 남은 입력 길이로 출력 길이를 계산한 뒤 끝에 패딩 문자('=')가 있으면 그 개수만큼 출력 길이를 줄이는데, 남은 입력이 1~3바이트뿐이면 출력 길이가 0인 상태에서 1~2를 빼게 되어 음수

d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.title_original: CVE-2026-114938: Critical vulnerability in OpenJDK JAVA
d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.excerpt: Cisco Talos is tracking the disclosure of a critical vulnerability in OpenJDK Java (CVE-2026-114938), dubbed “Java4Shell,” with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 that may lead to unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). This vulnerability can be triggered by sending a malformed Base64 input to affected JVMs, which can result in RCE. Details This vulnerability affects OpenJDK Java versions 17.0.6 and later running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions) support enabled. These vulnerabilities have already been tested against a suite of Java applications with success, but the attack surface is likely much larger as additional targets are tested and confirmed. This vulnerability does require a specific subset of processors that support AVX-512 VBMI; these include commonly deployed processors from both Intel and AMD, resulting in a large potential attack surface of vulnerable systems, including both on-premise and cloud environments. Cisco Talos would like to thank Calif.io for sharing the details of the vulnerability in advance of public disclosure . Observed exploitation Talos has not observed in-the-wild exploitation of this vulnerability yet. However, we anticipate probing attempts may pick up soon after public disclosure. Talos will continue to monitor for exploitation attempts and will provide updates accordingly. Recommendations and guidance Talos recommends applying the software update for this vulnerability. d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.title_ko: Cisco Talos, OpenJDK 원격 코드 실행 취약점 CVE-2026-114938 공개
d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.summary_ko: Cisco Talos는 OpenJDK Java 17.0.6 이상에서 조작된 Base64 입력으로 인증 없이 원격 코드 실행이 가능할 수 있는 취약점을 공개했다. AVX-512 VBMI가 활성화된 x86-64 환경이 대상이며 CVSS 4.0 점수는 9.2라고 설명했다. 실제 악용은 아직 관측되지 않았으며, 업데이트 적용이나 JVM의 AVX-512 사용 비활성화를 권고했다.
d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.background_ko: Talos에 따르면 AVX-512 VBMI가 활성화된 일부 x86-64 JVM에서 잘못된 Base64 입력을 처리할 때 원격 코드 실행이 발생할 수 있다.

fab5414136112eae4a905f9f.title_original: NEBench R1: a Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Nuclear Domain Competence in Large Language Models
fab5414136112eae4a905f9f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six LLMs were evaluated, with overall accuracy ranging from 34.0% to 73.9% across three distinct performance tiers. To assess reasoning quality, an LLM-based judge evaluated correctly answered responses using a multidimensional rubric. Although responses generally demonstrated strong problem comprehension, they scored lower in factual and procedural accuracy and distractor analysis, indicating that correct answers were not necessarily supported by technically sound justifications. Response clarity was also weakly indicative of technical quality. Furthermore, longer reasoning traces were associated with lower accuracy in both frontier reasoning models, suggesting that reasoning length may reflec

5a7df45b76f2d703d9c993d6.title_original: Chain-of-Thought Controllability Can Reduce Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
5a7df45b76f2d703d9c993d6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. Averaged across evaluations and CoT lengths, weighted by side-task-success counts, the CoT monitorability metric g-mean$^2$ falls from 0.94 for the base model to 0.68 for the model organism without a hiding instruction, and to 0.22 when explicitly instructed to hide. In intervention evaluations, explicit hiding often drives monitorability near zero. The effect extends to a Kimi-K2.6 model organism in agentic environments, though hidden objectives requiring extended reasoning or longer trajectories remain more monitorable than simple single-step side tasks. We further discover that targeted transparency prompts can substantially recover monitorability, sometimes surpassing the base model. These model organisms provide a testbed for studying monitorability failures and potential mi

45df6ff7508c243436f9e515.title_original: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
45df6ff7508c243436f9e515.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep networks score near 99% on the MSTAR vehicle benchmark, and the newer ATRNet-STAR benchmark was built to be harder. We ask how much of these scores comes from the vehicle itself. With a modern network (ConvNeXt-Small, 3 seeds) we first reproduce the known MSTAR result: with the central 96x96 pixels zeroed out, accuracy is still 73.3% (chance 10%). The same shortcut is present in ATRNet-STAR, which was collected across several scenes: with the vehicle removed, accuracy is 63.3% on the 40-class SOC split (chance 2.5%). Under the official scene-change split, the background stops helping and starts hurting. Accuracy is 22.8% on full chips and 30.8% when only the vehicle is shown. A SAR foundation model, SARATR-X, leans on the background more than ConvNeXt does (+4 to +6 points with the vehicle removed, in every seed) and does not solve the scene change. We then hold the amount of training data fixed and vary the depression angles used for training. Accuracy is set mainly by the gap to the nearest training angle: 57% at 15 degrees, 39% at 30 degrees and 26% at 45 degrees. Adding more training angles does not help. Finally, when most classes have training images at the test angle and a few do not, the missing classes do worse than when no class has them: 9.0% instead of 22.4% at a 45-degree gap. 0f5591fcec321237fda4c4c3.title_original: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
0f5591fcec321237fda4c4c3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. Given access to the full research transcript and the ability to run experiments, human auditors mostly fail to distinguish sabotaged from benign research: they achieve an AUROC of 0.59, not significantly better than chance, and fully identify the specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. Despite not being allowed to run experiments, the best frontier models outperform human auditors (Fable 5.1: AUROC 0.73, 32% full identification) within noise and weaker models perform comparably. When the saboteur chooses which experiments are attacked, rather than being required to sabotage every question given, sabotage identification drops further. Our results suggest that research sabotage by expert-level agents is difficult to detect with current auditing methods and provide a new setting for studying research sabotage.

3bbe0aeb2381d53c7fe8c9e8.title_original: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
3bbe0aeb2381d53c7fe8c9e8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. Given its weights, graded answers and the ability to run itself, a 27B model diagnoses its failure and edits the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on 490 problems it never saw, in a test fixed in advance, and another session's edit also makes it significantly better. It keeps getting better: it submits an edit only when its own tests support it, each edit replacing the last, and over its first eight such sessions its accuracy only rises. Unlike test-time scaling, the gain persists in its weights and adds no cost per answer; unlike training, it needs no pre- or post-training infrastructure, only an open model and hours on one GPU. It repairs a damaged copy of itself: it locates the corrupted matrix and rewrites it with values of its own, never reading the undamaged weights; found on text math problems alone, the repair lifts the copy on six image benchmarks it never saw from 7% to 70% accuracy, 83% of the undamaged model's.
