CVE-2026-108318.description: Tanium addressed an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in Tanium Server.

CVE-2026-108319.description: Tanium addressed a time-of-check time-of-use race condition vulnerability in Tanium Server.

CVE-2026-108320.description: Tanium addressed an improper access controls vulnerability in Tanium Server.

CVE-2026-108321.description: Tanium addressed an improper access controls vulnerability in Tanium Server.

CVE-2026-108323.description: Tanium addressed an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in Tanium Client.

CVE-2026-108761.description: The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to second-order SQL Injection via the user profile description field in all Free versions up to, and including, 1.26.15 and all Premium versions up to, and including, 2.26.15. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to store a malicious payload that is written into a database backup and executed as SQL when an administrator later restores that backup. Successful exploitation can modify sensitive WordPress data and, on sites where plugin installation is available, lead to remote code execution through the installation and activation of an attacker-controlled plugin.

CVE-2026-110009.description: The Unzer Payments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 2.2.1. The vulnerability exists because the Google Pay Express Checkout endpoint (`/?wc-api=google_pay_express`), handled by `startCheckoutDataWithNormalizedCustomerData`, accepts an attacker-controlled `paymentData.email` value and passes it to `createOrGetGuestCustomer()`, which resolves the submitted email to any existing WordPress user via `get_user_by('email', ...)` and then calls `wp_set_current_user()` and `wp_set_auth_cookie()` for the resolved user ID without verifying ownership of the email address, a password, a nonce, an authentication token, or any proof of payment from the payment provider. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as any existing WordPress user — including administrators — by submitting that user's known email address, receiving valid `wordpress_logged_in_*` session cookies for the targeted account and achieving full site takeover. The endpoint is entirely unprotected with no capability check, nonce validation, or payment-provider signature verification applied, and administrator email addresses are frequently discoverable via the WordPress REST API user enumeration endpoint (`/wp-json/wp/v2/users`), author archive pages, Gravatar lookups, or site contact footers.

CVE-2026-110811.description: The Trust Payments Gateway for WooCommerce (JavaScript Library) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.8. The vulnerability exists because the `new_customer_account()` function stores the raw return value of `wp_create_user()` — including a `WP_Error` object returned on username collision — into the order's `tp_userid` post meta before the `is_wp_error()` guard is evaluated; the `add_customer_details_to_thankyou_page()` callback subsequently reads that meta and casts it with `(int)`, causing PHP to coerce any object to integer `1`, after which `wp_set_current_user(1)` and `wp_set_auth_cookie(1)` are called unconditionally. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to authenticate as WordPress user ID 1 — the bootstrap site administrator or, on multisite, a network super-admin — by supplying the `new_username` parameter matching any existing login during checkout and visiting the resulting thank-you page. Exploitation requires the Trust Payments gateway to be active and the attacker to complete a paid order on their own account; the ID 1 administrator username is additionally enumerable via standard WordPress user enumeration techniques.

CVE-2026-115814.description: The Kirki – Freeform Page Builder, Website Builder & Customizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (title attribute of <abbr>)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.4.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to run the Kirki Convert (migration) workflow on a page containing the attacker's approved comment, as the browser-side DOM parser decodes the kses-allowed abbr title attribute value into a raw XSS payload that is then persisted without sanitization and later rendered unescaped. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

CVE-2026-115815.description: The rus to lat advanced plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to blind SQL Injection via the 'name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

CVE-2026-115826.description: The Multi Step for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.1 via the '_cf7mls_db_form_data_id' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to permanently delete arbitrary stored Contact Form 7 submissions from the database. Exploitation requires the companion CF7 Database plugin to be active and the per-form "Save every step, not just the final submission" option to be enabled.

CVE-2026-116519.description: The Geo Mashup plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author (comment form) / display_name (profile form)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.13.23 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The comment-author path requires the crafted comment to be approved before the payload is served to visitors; the subscriber-level path requires the plugin's user-location mapping feature to be enabled.

CVE-2026-116594.description: The Jeg Kit for Elementor – Powerful Addons for Elementor, Widgets & Templates for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'description' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful execution requires a published page containing both a Post Author widget in user_bio mode (rendering the attacker's biography) and any legitimate jkit_client_logo widget, so that client-logo.js is enqueued and the loadCarousel handler fires against the forged widget markup from the bio field.

CVE-2026-116758.description: The Advanced Country Blocker plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST_URI' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected script is stored via the advcb_live_activity transient on the init hook and executed when an administrator views the Live Monitor page, as the stored URI is unsafely concatenated into a double-quoted HTML title attribute and inserted into the DOM via jQuery .html().

CVE-2026-116764.description: The The GDPR Framework By Data443 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.2. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to delete all postmeta rows for every Easy Digital Downloads payment order on the site, destroying order metadata belonging to all customers. Exploitation requires that Easy Digital Downloads 2.x is active and the GDPR Framework's EDD compatibility option is enabled with a delete or delete_and_notify action configured.

CVE-2026-118068.description: The JobBoardWP – Job Board Listings and Submissions plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'job_description' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The plugin's default public submission workflow auto-provisions a jb_employer account for any visitor, meaning the effective entry point is unauthenticated — the custom role requirement imposes no real barrier on a stock install.

CVE-2026-118521.description: The Toolbox for Asgaros Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the replace_temp_pics function in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.4. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). This vulnerability is only reachable when the site administrator has enabled the Inline Image Upload feature (disabled by default).

CVE-2026-119631.description: The Kirki - Freeform Page Builder, Website Builder & Customizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Unauthorized Data Access in versions up to, and including, 6.4.1 via the `kirki_post_apis` AJAX action's `get-dynamic-content-batch` and `get-collection-batch` endpoints. This is due to the plugin opening these resolvers behind a site-wide, resource-unbound preview token (`EditorPreview::has_valid_token()`) that is NOT bound to the specific page the administrator intended to share, combined with the absence of any `list_users` or `can_user_read_post()` capability check inside `HelperFunctions::get_user_dynamic_content()` and `Collection::get_collection_batch()` — the equivalent checks ARE present on the plugin's own REST route (`FrontendRESTController::get_item_permissions_check()`). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers holding any valid read-only share link to extract from the entire user table every user's `user_email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `nickname`, `registered_date`, arbitrary string-valued `user_meta` (including custom keys such as `billing_phone`), and the e-mail address of every approved commenter — information that WordPress itself withholds from anonymous readers (served only in the `edit` context behind `list_users`).

CVE-2026-120564.description: The Search Everything plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in versions up to, and including, 8.1.9 via the search_everything AJAX action. The handler registered at `wp_ajax_search_everything` performs no capability check, no ownership check, and no nonce verification before running a WP_Query over `$_GET['s']` and returning the raw WP_Post objects — including the `post_password` field — as JSON. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to extract cleartext passwords for every password-protected post on the site and, when the plugin's draft/attachment/metadata search options are enabled by an administrator, to read draft and pending post contents they otherwise have no capability to view.

CVE-2026-122042.description: WarehousePG (WHPG) 6.27.1 through 6.27.7 and 7.2.1 through 7.6.1 are affected by an out-of-bounds write vulnerability (CWE-787) in gpfdist, the file server used to load and unload external tables. When gpfdist attaches a request to a session, it sizes two internal arrays from the client-supplied X-GP-SEGMENT-COUNT header and writes to them at the index given by the X-GP-SEGMENT-ID header, without checking that the index is non-negative and smaller than the count (CWE-129). gpfdist does not authenticate callers unless gpfdists is used with client certificate verification, so an attacker who can reach the gpfdist port can crash it with a single HTTP request, failing every external table load or unload that uses that gpfdist instance. gpfdist is normally reachable only from the cluster's internal network.

CVE-2026-123123.description: An attacker that is able to send a crafted network packet to the affected component may trigger an integer overflow during module size validation. This may cause insufficient bounds checking and result in out-of-bounds memory reads, potentially leading to a denial of service condition due to process termination.

CVE-2026-123419.description: The immonex Kickstart plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 1.19.0 via the 'inx-r-cidata (JSON blob containing 'template' and 'template_folders')' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The filename-level sanitization that strips dot-slash sequences applies only to the template filename component, not to the attacker-supplied template_folders directory paths, rendering it ineffective against directory traversal via that parameter.

CVE-2026-125053.description: The WEB-Translation – eTranslation Multilingual plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit requires that at least one secondary language is configured in the plugin and that comments are open on the target post; because the stored payload contains no literal HTML brackets at save-time, WordPress core KSES filtering does not remove it, and the malicious script is only materialized when a visitor loads the post under a secondary-language URL slug.

CVE-2026-125999.description: The Widget Manager Light plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'posts' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.18 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

CVE-2026-126131.description: The WP Instant Feeds plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[images][][url]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The cache-write AJAX endpoint is accessible to unauthenticated users because the only access control is a nonce check against a nonce minted for uid 0 and freely emitted on any front-end page rendering a feed via wp_localize_script, making it harvestable by any unauthenticated visitor.

CVE-2026-126763.description: In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 1.6 to 2.0.22 and 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, an MQTT v5.0 client connecting with a will-delay-interval that subsequently disconnects with a shorter interval causes all delayed wills to be suppressed.

CVE-2026-129323.description: The Masteriyo LMS – LMS Course Builder, Quizzes & Certificates plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.5.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. On a default install, any unauthenticated visitor can self-register as a Masteriyo Student through the plugin's public /account/signup/ form without administrator approval, granting them the publish_course_reviews capability required to submit reviews and exploit this vulnerability.

CVE-2026-130014.description: The Team VCard generator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.0 via the 'photo' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information.

CVE-2026-132138.description: A flaw was found in cyrus-sasl. When processing authentication requests using the Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism (SCRAM), a remote attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference by submitting unexpected channel-binding data. This causes the server process to crash before validating authentication proofs, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

CVE-2026-92535.description: The Make Connector plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.6 via the include_custom_fields. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract arbitrary admin-selected user, post, comment, and term metadata exposed via core REST endpoints — including active session tokens with source IP, user-agent, login and expiry timestamps, capability sets, and any other admin-selected private meta keys including protected underscore-prefixed entries. This is exploitable because the plugin's meta picker queries all meta keys from the database without filtering, offering protected underscore-prefixed keys such as session_tokens and wp_capabilities for administrator selection; if any such keys are selected, their values become readable without any credentials.

CVE-2026-95787.description: Vulnerabilities in the PAPI protocol of AOS-10 could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to circumvent existing authentication controls. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to gain administrative access, modify system configurations, and access or manipulate sensitive data.

CVE-2026-95788.description: An unauthenticated buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the underlying operating system of AOS-10 or AOS-8 and could allow an unauthenticated adjacent attacker to conduct a denial of service attack. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to disrupt the availability of the affected system, with a limited impact to the integrity of the affected component.

CVE-2026-95789.description: Command injection vulnerability in the affected interface of AOS-10 or AOS-8 could allow an authenticated remote attacker to perform command injection only on certain impacted devices. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to execute unauthorized arbitrary commands with the privileges of the affected mechanism on the underlying operating system.

CVE-2026-95790.description: A vulnerability in the web-based management interface of network device management systems of AOS-8 Mobility Controllers could allow an authenticated remote attacker to bypass authorization controls. Successful exploitation could allow a low-privilege attacker to read sensitive configuration data potentially leading to unauthorized network access and further compromise of network security.

CVE-2026-96665.description: The SendPress Newsletters plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'sp_firstname' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.26.1.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The public subscriber-management route uses an unsigned, forgeable base64-encoded JSON token, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to impersonate any subscriber and obtain a valid nonce — bypassing the POST handler's only access control check.

CVE-2026-96841.description: The ITRO Popup Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'custom_html' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.2.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is only exploitable by low-privileged roles such as Subscriber when an administrator has explicitly granted that role access to the plugin settings page via the plugin's role selection option.

2d68b5ab513fd37b5cf53768.excerpt: 마이크로소프트(MS)가 오픈AI와 앤트로픽의 첨단 모델에 근접한 코딩 성능을 훨씬 낮은 비용으로 구현한 자체 AI 모델 'MAI 코드 2(MAI Code 2)'를 공개했다. 사이버 보안과 AI 에이전트의 판단 작업에 특화한 모델도 함께 선보이며, 외부 AI 모델에 대한 의존도를 줄이고 자체 모델 경쟁력을 강화하고 나섰다.MS는 17일(현지시간) 미국 샌프란시스코에서 열린 연례 기술 행사 '이그나이트 2026'에서 코딩 전문 모델 'MAI 코드 2'와 경량형 'MAI 코드 2 플래시(MAI Code 2 Flash)', 보안 전문 모델
2d68b5ab513fd37b5cf53768.title_ko: MS, 코딩·보안 특화 자체 AI 모델 공개…성능·비용 경쟁력 강조
2d68b5ab513fd37b5cf53768.summary_ko: MS가 코딩 모델 ‘MAI 코드 2’와 경량형 플래시, 보안 특화 모델 및 에이전트 판단 모델을 공개했다. MS는 MAI 코드 2가 클로드 오퍼스 5.5 대비 96% 성능을 5% 비용으로 제공한다고 밝혔으나, 이는 자체 평가이며 비용 비교에는 50% 프로모션 가격이 반영됐다.
2d68b5ab513fd37b5cf53768.background_ko: MS는 외부 AI 모델에 대한 의존도를 낮추고 자체 모델 경쟁력을 강화하기 위해 업무별 특화 모델 개발을 확대하고 있다.

curation.reason_ko: MS가 자체 코딩·보안 모델을 공개했으며 성능·비용 수치는 자체 평가와 프로모션 조건을 구별해야 한다.

09a2ca5ec574bc77f2190a31.excerpt: In this article A new cyber stack, built to fight AI with AI Delivering agentic security at Microsoft Ignite Secure your foundations Defend with agents Secure agentic insiders Changing how security work gets done Explore what's new A year ago, finding a serious, exploitable vulnerability was slow and expensive work done by elite security researchers. That’s no longer true. Over the past 12 months, frontier AI models have become remarkably good at discovering and exploiting software vulnerabilities, and similar levels of capability are quickly becoming available in open weights models with limited cyber guardrails. Attacks that once required specialized resources are now within reach of almost anyone. We saw what that looks like in a single week this fall when PHP disclosed two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities, flaws that let an attacker take control of a server with a single request over the internet. 1 At the time of disclosure, tens of millions of internet-facing PHP services were running affected versions. Nearly two weeks later, about 29 million services remained vulnerable. Behind those servers are banks, healthcare providers, energy companies, and much of the infrastructure the internet runs on. And that same day brought five other major disclosures across the industry. 71853ef952e2bfb0eef37813.title_original: The risks of device code authentication for AI coding agents
71853ef952e2bfb0eef37813.excerpt: In this article From a familiar phishing technique to an AI coding agent How the attack works One approval, four ways the impact can spread Turning a phishing attempt into a Defender signal Mitigation and protection guidance References Learn More Device code phishing has become a recurring route to account takeover. Instead of stealing a password, an attacker persuades someone to approve a sign-in on a legitimate site simply by entering a code. The resulting access often can reach email, files, or other cloud services, depending on the account and the permissions granted. Notable earlier campaigns such as EvilTokens show how readily this technique can be scaled to do real damage. Microsoft worked hard with partners in industry and law enforcement to disrupt EvilTokens in September 2026. That led us to a different question: what else can an attacker do with a phished device code authorization? What happens when the same trick targets an AI agent rather than a mailbox? We used GitHub Copilot CLI as an illustrative example. Depending on its configuration, it can work with code, run commands on a user’s machine, retain context across sessions, and allow an active session to be steered remotely. Like many command-line tools, it supports the OAuth device flow for sign-in. c6d97c03dd402eb660c3e76d.title_original: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
c6d97c03dd402eb660c3e76d.excerpt: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely , a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC , CNN , Equifax , Ledger and Zoom , was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content. The Zoom.com homepage loading the malicious JavaScript file from Optimizely. Image: blog.report-uri.com. Click to enlarge. According to a blog post from the security firm Report URI , on November 16 malicious JavaScript code was served to visitors of 178 organizations through Optimizely’s platform. Report URI researcher Scott Helme wrote that the payload delivered by the malicious Javascript was rebuilt 26 times during the day, dropping a multi-purpose malware kit that could steal payment card data, cookies and screenshots, and swap any cryptocurrency payment addresses for the attacker’s. Helme noted the affected websites also served exploit code custom made to attack known vulnerabilities in older Apple iPhone and iPad devices. 93243ae5929fdfb9c7d9c5fb.title_original: 자바(Java), 인증 없이 원격 코드 실행 가능한 ‘Java4Shell’ 취약점(CVE-2026-114938) 긴급 업데이트 권고
93243ae5929fdfb9c7d9c5fb.excerpt: 생성형 AI 제작 이미지 오라클(Oracle)과 OpenJDK가 자바(Java) 실행 환경에서 발견된 원격 코드 실행 취약점(CVE-2026-114938, 일명 Java4Shell)에 대한 보안 업데이트를 배포했습니다. 이번 취약점은 자바 가상 머신(JVM)인 HotSpot이 Base64 디코딩을 빠르게 처리하기 위해 사용하는 하드웨어 가속 코드에서 발생하는 '힙 메모리 경계 밖 쓰기(Out-of-Bounds Write)' 결함입니다. AVX-512 명령어를 지원하는 x86-64 서버에서 끝부분에 패딩 문자('=')가 붙은 조작된 Base64 문자열을 디코딩할 때, 출력 길이가 음수로 잘못 계산되면서 결과를 저장하는 배열의 범위를 넘어 메모리를 덮어쓰게 됩니다. Base64 디코딩은 로그인 인증, 파일 업로드 등 웹 서비스의 일반적인 기능에서 폭넓게 사용되기 때문에, 공격자는 인증 없이 원격에서 조작된 요청을 보내는 것만으로 서버의 메모리를 손상시키고 임의 코드를 실행할 수 있습니다. 국가사이버안보센터도 세부 내용 공개에 앞서 보안 권고를 발표한 만큼 자바를 사용하는 서버 운영자분들의 신속한 업데이트를 권고 드립니다. 취약점 개요 CVE CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell) 영향 컴포넌트 OpenJDK HotSpot 컴파일러(hotspot/compiler) x86-64용 Base64 디코딩 인트린직(AVX-512 VBMI 가속 코드), java.util.Base64 기본/URL 디코더 취약점 유형 정수 언더플로로 인한 힙 메모리 경계 밖 쓰기(Out-of-Bounds Write) 인증 없이 원격에서 메모리 손상, 정보 유출 및 임의 코드 실행 가능 심각도 High (CVSS v3.1 8.1) 영향 대상 OpenJDK 17.0.6 이상 및 이를 기반으로 한 자바 17/21/25/27 배포판 AVX-512 VBMI를 지원하는 x86-64 CPU에서 실행되는 경우에 한함 (ARM64 해당 없음) 실제 악용 실제 공격에 악용된 사례는 보고되지 않음 (2026. 11. 18. 기준) 발견자가 취약점 재현 코드를 공개했으며, 제품별 공격 코드는 비공개 조치 Oracle Java SE 및 OpenJDK 배포판의 11월 보안 업데이트 적용 후 자바 애플리케이션 재시작 취약점 발생 원인 자바의 JIT 컴파일러는 자주 실행되는 표준 라이브러리 기능 일부를 CPU에 최적화된 어셈블리 코드로 바꿔 실행하는데, 이를 인트린직(Intrinsic)이라고 합니다. java.util.Base64 의 디코딩 기능도 그중 하나로, OpenJDK 17.0.6부터 AVX-512 명령어를 지원하는 x86-64 CPU에서는 64바이트 단위로 데이터를 한 번에 처리하는 가속 코드가 사용됩니다. 문제는 이 가속 코드가 입력의 마지막 부분을 처리하는 방식에 있습니다. 가속 코드는 남은 입력 길이로 출력 길이를 계산한 뒤 끝에 패딩 문자('=')가 있으면 그 개수만큼 출력 길이를 줄이는데, 남은 입력이 1~3바이트뿐이면 출력 길이가 0인 상태에서 1~2를 빼게 되어 음수

d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.title_original: CVE-2026-114938: Critical vulnerability in OpenJDK JAVA
d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.excerpt: Cisco Talos is tracking the disclosure of a critical vulnerability in OpenJDK Java (CVE-2026-114938), dubbed “Java4Shell,” with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 that may lead to unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). This vulnerability can be triggered by sending a malformed Base64 input to affected JVMs, which can result in RCE. Details This vulnerability affects OpenJDK Java versions 17.0.6 and later running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions) support enabled. These vulnerabilities have already been tested against a suite of Java applications with success, but the attack surface is likely much larger as additional targets are tested and confirmed. This vulnerability does require a specific subset of processors that support AVX-512 VBMI; these include commonly deployed processors from both Intel and AMD, resulting in a large potential attack surface of vulnerable systems, including both on-premise and cloud environments. Cisco Talos would like to thank Calif.io for sharing the details of the vulnerability in advance of public disclosure . Observed exploitation Talos has not observed in-the-wild exploitation of this vulnerability yet. However, we anticipate probing attempts may pick up soon after public disclosure. Talos will continue to monitor for exploitation attempts and will provide updates accordingly. Recommendations and guidance Talos recommends applying the software update for this vulnerability. d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.title_ko: Cisco Talos, OpenJDK 원격 코드 실행 취약점 CVE-2026-114938 공개
d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.summary_ko: Cisco Talos는 OpenJDK Java 17.0.6 이상에서 조작된 Base64 입력으로 인증 없이 원격 코드 실행이 가능할 수 있는 취약점을 공개했다. AVX-512 VBMI가 활성화된 x86-64 환경이 대상이며 CVSS 4.0 점수는 9.2라고 설명했다. 실제 악용은 아직 관측되지 않았으며, 업데이트 적용이나 JVM의 AVX-512 사용 비활성화를 권고했다.
d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.background_ko: Talos에 따르면 AVX-512 VBMI가 활성화된 일부 x86-64 JVM에서 잘못된 Base64 입력을 처리할 때 원격 코드 실행이 발생할 수 있다.

fab5414136112eae4a905f9f.title_original: NEBench R1: a Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Nuclear Domain Competence in Large Language Models
fab5414136112eae4a905f9f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six LLMs were evaluated, with overall accuracy ranging from 34.0% to 73.9% across three distinct performance tiers. To assess reasoning quality, an LLM-based judge evaluated correctly answered responses using a multidimensional rubric. Although responses generally demonstrated strong problem comprehension, they scored lower in factual and procedural accuracy and distractor analysis, indicating that correct answers were not necessarily supported by technically sound justifications. Response clarity was also weakly indicative of technical quality. Furthermore, longer reasoning traces were associated with lower accuracy in both frontier reasoning models, suggesting that reasoning length may reflec

5a7df45b76f2d703d9c993d6.title_original: Chain-of-Thought Controllability Can Reduce Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
5a7df45b76f2d703d9c993d6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. Averaged across evaluations and CoT lengths, weighted by side-task-success counts, the CoT monitorability metric g-mean$^2$ falls from 0.94 for the base model to 0.68 for the model organism without a hiding instruction, and to 0.22 when explicitly instructed to hide. In intervention evaluations, explicit hiding often drives monitorability near zero. The effect extends to a Kimi-K2.6 model organism in agentic environments, though hidden objectives requiring extended reasoning or longer trajectories remain more monitorable than simple single-step side tasks. We further discover that targeted transparency prompts can substantially recover monitorability, sometimes surpassing the base model. These model organisms provide a testbed for studying monitorability failures and potential mi

45df6ff7508c243436f9e515.title_original: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
45df6ff7508c243436f9e515.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep networks score near 99% on the MSTAR vehicle benchmark, and the newer ATRNet-STAR benchmark was built to be harder. We ask how much of these scores comes from the vehicle itself. With a modern network (ConvNeXt-Small, 3 seeds) we first reproduce the known MSTAR result: with the central 96x96 pixels zeroed out, accuracy is still 73.3% (chance 10%). The same shortcut is present in ATRNet-STAR, which was collected across several scenes: with the vehicle removed, accuracy is 63.3% on the 40-class SOC split (chance 2.5%). Under the official scene-change split, the background stops helping and starts hurting. Accuracy is 22.8% on full chips and 30.8% when only the vehicle is shown. A SAR foundation model, SARATR-X, leans on the background more than ConvNeXt does (+4 to +6 points with the vehicle removed, in every seed) and does not solve the scene change. We then hold the amount of training data fixed and vary the depression angles used for training. Accuracy is set mainly by the gap to the nearest training angle: 57% at 15 degrees, 39% at 30 degrees and 26% at 45 degrees. Adding more training angles does not help. Finally, when most classes have training images at the test angle and a few do not, the missing classes do worse than when no class has them: 9.0% instead of 22.4% at a 45-degree gap. 0f5591fcec321237fda4c4c3.title_original: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
0f5591fcec321237fda4c4c3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. Given access to the full research transcript and the ability to run experiments, human auditors mostly fail to distinguish sabotaged from benign research: they achieve an AUROC of 0.59, not significantly better than chance, and fully identify the specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. Despite not being allowed to run experiments, the best frontier models outperform human auditors (Fable 5.1: AUROC 0.73, 32% full identification) within noise and weaker models perform comparably. When the saboteur chooses which experiments are attacked, rather than being required to sabotage every question given, sabotage identification drops further. Our results suggest that research sabotage by expert-level agents is difficult to detect with current auditing methods and provide a new setting for studying research sabotage.

3bbe0aeb2381d53c7fe8c9e8.title_original: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
3bbe0aeb2381d53c7fe8c9e8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. Given its weights, graded answers and the ability to run itself, a 27B model diagnoses its failure and edits the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on 490 problems it never saw, in a test fixed in advance, and another session's edit also makes it significantly better. It keeps getting better: it submits an edit only when its own tests support it, each edit replacing the last, and over its first eight such sessions its accuracy only rises. Unlike test-time scaling, the gain persists in its weights and adds no cost per answer; unlike training, it needs no pre- or post-training infrastructure, only an open model and hours on one GPU. It repairs a damaged copy of itself: it locates the corrupted matrix and rewrites it with values of its own, never reading the undamaged weights; found on text math problems alone, the repair lifts the copy on six image benchmarks it never saw from 7% to 70% accuracy, 83% of the undamaged model's. And the ability

b1e48c0fcf92a241e6b4e71b.title_original: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
b1e48c0fcf92a241e6b4e71b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speculative-diffusion decoding uses a small parallel drafter model to generate b draft tokens in one forward pass, which then undergo parallel verification via a larger target model. Faster inference can be achieved when multiple draft tokens pass verification simultaneously. Recent parallel draft architectures (DFlash, DSpark) improve draft quality by conditioning on rich features computed by the target, through a mechanism known as feature encoding. However, standard feature encoding mechanisms have three limitations: (1) they are lossy, applying encoding projections that are destructive to the underlying target feature-space via a discovered effect known as residual mixing, (2) they are memory-less, with no record of previously processed proposals, and (3) they utilize features sampled uniformly from across the target layers, omitting important hidden states. To address these issues, we propose Mixture-of-Features Attention (MoFA), a lightweight feature-encoding approach equipped with a working memory that encodes previously rejected proposals. Leveraging MoFA, rejection memory, and a set of further enhancements, including 2-tap causal convolutions, prefix-only cross-attention, and non-uniform target layer selection, the final architecture, DNeo, achieves 1.3x faster generation speed than SoTA (DFlash-2) without impacting drafter footprint or generation quality. DNeo marks a new state of the art in high quality, fast LLM infe

033a6ad1a289d5b0bd9f6301.title_original: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
033a6ad1a289d5b0bd9f6301.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern sensing systems generate large volumes of heterogeneous data streams from multiple sensor modalities, increasing reliance on datacenters for computation, artificial intelligence/superintelligence (AI/SI) inference, and AI/SI training. Each sensor stream may have different network and compute requirements depending on its type and data volume. However, current wireless systems typically allocate resources at the device level, leading to contention among co-located sensor streams, where bulk data transfers may starve latency-critical telemetry. To this end, this paper introduces Sensor Slicing (SL). SL provides deterministic, medium access control (MAC)-level isolation for individual sensors within a single user equipment (UE) in open radio access networks (O-RAN). Using agentic coding techniques, SL is implemented in two O-RAN-compliant packages, reducing development time by 400 times (2 h 40 min [OCUDU] vs. 6.5 weeks [OAI]), 228-fold fewer human prompts (4 vs. 913), and less than half the tokens (0.64B vs. 1.43B). An associated end-to-end framework, SLED, is implemented to establish per-sensor radio and network isolation across edge, campus, and remote high-performance computing (HPC) tiers. Over-the-air wireless experiments demonstrate that while conventional network slicing causes critical delays to increase more than 2,300-fold under high traffic load, SLED maintains stable latency. Scaling evaluations on the two RAN s

bc941556ae4b3efb0873b924.title_original: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
bc941556ae4b3efb0873b924.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A reasoning model that has reached a correct answer can lose it by continuing to think. Deciding whether to stop means comparing two probabilities at the same point of a chain: that the answer the model would give if stopped now is correct (its commitment), and that the answer it will finish with is correct (its verdict). We show that the verdict alone, which is what final-correctness probes estimate, cannot make this comparison. As a forecast of a fixed outcome it has no predictable drift, whether continuing helps or hurts. The commitment-verdict gap equals the expected remaining change in answer quality and the accuracy gained by stopping. A second identity splits any accuracy-versus-budget curve into answer change within chains and change in which chains are still running. We measure both on MATH-500. At all 379 points where DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B holds a correct answer, selected without regard to how its chain ends, continuing loses 3.6 points on average (95% CI [2.2, 5.2]), and the loss concentrates in a few problems. In six reasoning models from three families, on MATH-500 and OlympiadBench and with budgets up to 16,384 tokens, declining accuracy curves come from which chains remain, while the chains still reasoning keep or improve their answers. An oracle stopping rule gains at most +1.8 and +2.5 points at 1.5B and 7B. The framework says what to measure before building a stopping rule.

6f99205928973f0acace1ab3.title_original: Honest Brokers in AI Regulation: How Public Comments Introduce Evidence to Regulators
6f99205928973f0acace1ab3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The regulation of Artificial Intelligence is susceptible to various forms of capture by industry actors that hold undue influence over the policymaking process, due in part to their information advantage in developing these technologies. In the following paper, we investigate the roles of public commenters in providing evidence to potential regulation in the USA. We build a corpus of 40 potential regulations, and 2,664 public comments submitted by a variety of stakeholders. We computationally process these texts to extract evidence meant to inform regulators, in the form of formal citations and informal references. We find significant differences in the type and amount of evidence supplied: Holding comment length constant, business commenters introduce altogether less evidence, and government, university, and civil society commenters provide significantly more research and legal sources. The publication status of cited research is nearly evenly split, with preprints and peer-reviewed articles being introduced by commenters of all types. We further explore patterns of self-citation and find that while it is prevalent amongst all groups, a small cluster of organizations account for over half of all self-citations in our corpus. Our findings complicate a narrative that public comments alone are means to information capture. We interpret these results in terms of the role that commenters attempt to play in the policymaking process-b

72f03d377c75bc4253a36853.title_original: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
72f03d377c75bc4253a36853.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. We present DiscoveryAgent, a domain-agnostic, scientist-centric system that combines autonomous investigation with scientist-directed hypothesis steering. Scientists select, refine, or replace hypotheses between research rounds, while audit agents interrogate checkpointed records to trace claims, reproduce analyses, and inform subsequent decisions. Across two predictive modeling tasks, DiscoveryAgent produced the best variable-star classifier among evaluated baselines and, with scientist steering, a protein variant-effect predictor surpassed by only one of 106 ProteinGym baselines. We develop a rigorous checkpointing system that enables highly capable audit agents, a scalable form of oversight for agentic research. Audit agents autonomously identify errors at higher rates than previous AI scientist agents, and scientists collaborating with audit agents identify 14x more valid errors versus scientists performing manual review. In three case studies led by domain experts across physical science, social science, and life science, we developed a multimodal photometric-redshift estimator that resolves complementary failures of images and photometry, achieving 0.971 AUROC for low-redshift classification; documented an 83% rise in Florida homeowners-insurance

e3329e7c04f303c4147e6d8d.title_original: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web
e3329e7c04f303c4147e6d8d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are moving from isolated assistants toward autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and coordinate with others, motivating an emerging Agentic Web of independently developed agents and services. Realizing this vision requires agent behavior to move across creators, hosts, and runtimes without coupling publication to a particular execution environment or transferring authority over user resources. We introduce WebAgents, which unbundles these roles through a signed agent.pkg that carries portable workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements. An OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime verifies the package, obtains authorization, and binds it at run time to user-controlled models, tools, permissions, and budgets, while hosts distribute the public program and may retain private services server-side. We demonstrate this contract with three unrelated workflows executed unchanged under local and API-backed models, including literature review with live services and a website-published travel agent using semantic tools and user-selected personal resources. In a controlled suite, WebAgents explicitly blocks all 716 injected contract violations while accepting all 295 matched benign controls, with median automated pre-execution processing below 0.5 s for all three packages. We conclude by outlining a path toward NANDA-based discovery and interoperable package ecosystems while retaining execution author

4b527441d71892fe43b9e5a0.title_original: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants
4b527441d71892fe43b9e5a0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personal assistants accumulate months of conversations, but today's long-term memory stacks put derivation or selection between a question and its evidence. In a system-level comparison on LongMemEval, two commercial assistants scored well below the same model reading the history offline [1], consistent with, but not isolating, content loss between write and read. We propose KV-LTM: a memory tier storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering by restoring cached sessions and appending the question. KV-LTM is complementary to, not a replacement for, retrieval and indexing. Text is the memory of record; the cache is a recompute-free prefill accelerator, degrading gracefully to text. We specify the design: storage record, budget-derived retention, append-only read path, and bounded aggregation. We size it analytically: across pinned BF16 full-attention (GQA) and latent-cached MLA configurations, per-token state spans approximately 31K-328K bytes (the pinned KDA+MLA hybrid differs: approximately 8.1K bytes/token plus a fixed per-session recurrent term), giving approximately 0.34-3.6 TB per user-year at a declared 30K-token/day scenario, against approximately 49 MB of raw text; per-query cost is modelled as regime-conditional transfer, attention, decode, aggregation, and compute. We define an evaluation protocol needing no persistent-cache implementation for logical QA evaluation: per-session

71bba7c66628b4e6799ccfbc.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Counterfactual explanations are often seen as counterfactual conditionals under closest-world semantics, requiring one to reason over all minimally distant counterexamples. In contrast, formal XAI typically relies on feature-based abductive explanations (AXps) and contrastive explanations (CXps), which admit efficient computation and a minimal hitting-set duality. This paper bridges these perspectives by (i) characterizing closest-world counterfactual explanations explicitly as a disjunctive normal form over all minimally distant counterexample instances, and (ii) introducing conjunctive counterfactual explanations (CFXps), a subclass of counterfactual antecedents restricted to conjunctions of feature literals that guarantee prediction change. The paper establishes structural results connecting CXps, AXps and CFXps: every CXp induces an AXp for its witness instance, and every CXp together with a witness AXp induces a CFXp whose support is precisely determined by that AXp. These theoretical results yield a modular approach for computing CFXps using existing AXp/CXp machinery. Experiments on a representative set of benchmarks using tree ensembles and neural networks show that CFXp extraction is practically efficient. Compared with popular point-based counterfactual explainers, CFXps generally require no more feature changes and can guarantee the counterfactual prediction beyond a single instance.

2a80958456627ac75a941ca8.title_original: SkillBuffBench: Measuring What Agent Skills Contribute across Harnesses, Models, Skill Access Modes and Memory
2a80958456627ac75a941ca8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent Skills, file-based packages of procedural knowledge that a coding agent can discover and load on demand, are now shipped by every major agent harness, yet the evidence for how much they help comes almost entirely from settings in which the right Skill is hand-picked for the task and the agent starts from a blank slate. Neither holds in deployment, where an agent chooses from whatever library happens to be installed and frequently carries memory from earlier work. We present SkillBuffBench, a benchmark and paired evaluation protocol that treats Skill access as a three-level factor (no Skill, a curated Skill, and automatic invocation from an installed library), crosses it with memory (off and on), with four agent harnesses and with multiple models (the state-of-the-art proprietary models from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI, and the state-of-the-art open-weight models from Chinese providers), every model being run under every harness, and evaluates the result on research tasks contributed by domain experts together with the Skills they use, currently in materials science and biology, with the suite extended on a rolling basis. Every run is marked by a deterministic verifier; uncertainty is reported with a paired, task-level bootstrap; and cost, agent rounds and wall-clock time are reported alongside the score rather than folded into it. This version of the paper describes the design of the benchmark, its evaluation protocol and

4b08beade3f524a68a4f8ddd.title_original: What Does an Agent Need? Bundle-Aware Agent Resource Composition
4b08beade3f524a68a4f8ddd.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent resource's value depends on its backbone and companion resources and is known only after execution. Token-based generators remain tied to their training catalog, while independent resource scoring misses complementarities and reused bundles target other tasks. We formulate Task-Conditioned Agent Resource Composition (AgentComposition): jointly selecting a backbone model and a tool-skill bundle to maximize end-to-end execution utility. Our Retrieval-Grounded Bundle-Aware Agent Generation retrieves candidate resources and past configurations of similar tasks. A fine-tuned generator reads resource descriptions and recombines candidates through constrained beam search, allowing new resources without retraining. A bundle-aware critic ranks complete configurations using a large language model (LLM) teacher and historically successful configurations as execution proxies, and adapts to execution feedback when available. We evaluate reference recovery, offline execution with judged and native rewards, and online recommendation with real execution, building AgentSelect-Exec with 5,060 executed configurations. Our method recovers the complete reference configuration within ten candidates for 67.73% of AgentSelect queries, nearly twice the strongest baseline, and leads all baselines on SkillsBench. The proxy-trained critic raises the top-ranked agent's execution score from 7.58 to 8.37 out of 10; execution feedback increases it to

c37ec54c3c7efe448b748c9a.title_original: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
c37ec54c3c7efe448b748c9a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. To test this belief, we ask two questions about such agents: does asking a model to think harder make it choose better products, and does the confidence it reports tell us the likelihood it may be wrong? We benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice benchmarks built from WebShop, Amazon's SQID and Wayfair's WANDS platforms to see if LLMs with more thinking power actually make better-quality product purchase decisions. Across all three benchmarks, we found that increasing the thinking effort does not increase decision quality in a statistically meaningful way. The same change in thinking effort raises stated confidence at a statistically significant level, so extra thinking buys confidence rather than correctness. We also measure the calibration of these models (how well their reported confidence percentage matches their true correctness percentage) in these tasks and show that most models are not well-calibrated at every effort level. We also find that errors are strongly shared: when one model errs in a task, several others tend to err on that same task. Furthermore, on tasks where several models al

c16e69baa4cd12ffb755970a.title_original: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem
c16e69baa4cd12ffb755970a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the solver we submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest on the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis. The solver is a single-file, standard-library Python program that combines (i) a constant-time insertion test based on latest-arrival slack, (ii) greedy insertion, local search and an Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) with simulated-annealing acceptance, and (iii) an exact route-selection engine that enumerates, for every taxi, the best feasible route for each request set and then solves the resulting set-packing problem by branch-and-bound strengthened with route-based large neighborhood search, Lagrangian bounds and reduced-cost fixing. The engine is chosen automatically from the instance size, and an independent verifier and a watchdog guarantee that a valid answer is always printed. On the official evaluation (38 scored instances, 5-minute limit) the solver obtained a total benefit of 487,237, finished every run within 277 s and used at most 279 MB; 28 of the 38 instances terminated well before the limit.

15503d9ccedeb5d4ac7cd6ee.title_original: MedGuardBench: A Patient-Oriented Benchmark for Personalized Guardrail Development
15503d9ccedeb5d4ac7cd6ee.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety is personal: the same action can be safe for one person but unsafe for another. Yet current guardrails judge content without considering who is affected. Using medication safety, we introduce \textit{patient-conditioned medication guarding}, which predicts a safety verdict and 17 risk categories from a patient profile and prescription. We release \textbf{MedGuardBench}, a drug-disjoint benchmark of 5{,}001 scenarios across 87 medications. We find that standard guardrails rely on surface cues, such as wording and profile presence, rather than patient facts. To address this, we develop \textit{personalized reasoning guardrails} with three components. \textbf{Personalized Reasoning Distillation} links risks to relevant patient fields. \textbf{Context Unrolling (CU)} makes models check each field themselves, reducing false alarms on most backbones; controls show that providing the check does not yield the same benefit. A \textbf{rule-based reward (guided GRPO)} improves unsafe recall and complex-risk detection, including allergies and adverse reactions, on some backbones, but increases false alarms on others. Our models outperform base models and matched no-profile controls in accuracy, while reducing false alarms relative to no-profile controls. Profile removal and swapping confirm that gains come from patient information, not fine-tuning alone.

02de2fcca97c16fdb0cc3703.title_original: Can You Undo It? Reversibility Classes for AI Agent Actions
02de2fcca97c16fdb0cc3703.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using AI agents change files, databases, access rights and public information, yet permission to call a tool does not establish whether a mistake can be undone. We present Reversibility Classes, a declared five-level vocabulary with argument-sensitive rules, conservative defaults and an explicit prior-state capture contract. The pinned implementation and evidence-linked registry cover 536 tools across 20 MCP servers. All 738 rule-case checks conform to declared expectations, while native annotation mapping differs from draft registry labels for 118 of 481 comparable tools. One AI-assisted reviewer approves 148 ratings, 75 matching the registry; this is not independent agreement. On 2,158 recorded runs, the implemented session guard gates the associated action in all 29 attributable attack-positive runs, compared with 18 for a read/write proxy, while adding nine approval points across 1,209 benign runs. Controlled file, Git, SQLite and three-browser experiments show that recovery depends on captured state, later changes, editor storage and recovery route, and expose a Git merge-state exception. The evidence supports making recovery assumptions explicit and testable. It does not establish registry-wide accuracy, reduced production harm or general recovery reliability.

fda5ad67e4789ad5299d6337.title_original: When Lower Harm Misleads: Auditing Concept Corrections
fda5ad67e4789ad5299d6337.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An expert who corrects a concept prediction, such as a BI-RADS descriptor in breast ultrasound, expects the diagnosis to improve. Objectives that reduce the harm of such corrections are judged by harm and accuracy, yet harm also falls when a model responds less to every correction or starts from a worse uncorrected prediction, the reference for harm. We propose a correction audit, a reproducible evaluation protocol that separates these explanations: it splits each correction into harm and useful gain on identical events, separates the starting prediction from the correction response, and compares objectives with amplitude baselines matched in source harm. On three breast-ultrasound sources, worst-case correction training, evaluated from the mean-case model's start, lowers harm but gives up more useful gain in all 21 source comparisons pooled over six seeds, raising the corrected negative log-likelihood (NLL); from the same start, selecting between the objectives by harm picks the less helpful model on all three sources. On CUB, a monotonic harm penalty at its reported weight lowers path-level harm in all 80 concept sets while raising the NLL in all 80, almost entirely before any correction. d4bb95c67faa4f760b5b670d.title_original: ATLAS-Finance: Benchmarking AI Agents in Realistic Banking Environments
d4bb95c67faa4f760b5b670d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Professional work involves under-specified assignments, where relevant information is spread across workplace applications and may conflict or change over time. To evaluate how well frontier agents can perform economically valuable work in such settings, we introduce ATLAS-Finance, a benchmark of 100 end-to-end investment-banking tasks across 13 simulated firms. As in real banking workflows, agents must search email, chat, calendars, notes, and files to identify requirements, gather information, reconcile conflicts/updates, and then build complex financial models. Tasks were developed by experienced bankers based on their real deal work and take them 15-30 hours to complete. Agent deliverables are evaluated with expert-authored rubrics (median: 124.5 criteria) covering financial rationale and results, spreadsheet construction, completeness, and formatting. Despite completing substantial portions of the requested work, current agents rarely produce correct deliverables. Across today's frontier models, the best ones (Claude Opus and Fable) pass fewer than 11% of tasks.

958167a5a0647ff1908b0d8d.title_original: EvoDisco: Strategy Discovery for Evolving Agent Memory
958167a5a0647ff1908b0d8d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents accumulate experience in memory, and how that memory evolves during interaction is as important as what it stores. Recent methods update memory online, yet both the operators that transform memory and the rules that select them remain fixed by design. We propose EvoDisco, which formulates agent memory evolution as evolutionary strategy discovery: the agent must discover which operator to apply, when to apply it, and how to instantiate it, rather than rewriting memory under a static operator schedule. A learnable policy conditions on the current memory state and recent task history, then selects and instantiates one of four semantic operators---Abstract, Refine, Bridge, and Reframe---which respectively compress related memories, decompose overloaded entries, connect weakly linked experiences, and reorganize retrieved reasoning chains. The policy is updated with a bi-level fitness. An inner signal scores each transformation using a retrieval-quality improvement regularized by memory complexity. An outer signal scores strategic efficacy over a window of past decisions, combining historical operator-utility regret, utility-prediction error, and selection diversity. Under a one-pass online plus frozen-transfer protocol on ALFWorld, WebShop, and LifelongAgentBench (OS and DB), EvoDisco improves over strong memory baselines including MemP and MemRL. The largest gains are on ALFWorld ($+8.8$ online / $+12.9$

46ce5255881e70f9b4b3815d.title_original: From Sorry to QED: Refining LLM Math Proofs via Angelic Execution
46ce5255881e70f9b4b3815d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can now generate Lean proof scripts that capture the high-level structure of many mathematical arguments. However, these scripts frequently fail on complex theorems: a single missing side condition or misapplied lemma can cause the prover to abort early and discard an otherwise viable proof outline. This paper presents MathEye, a framework that converts imperfect LLM-generated proof scripts into fully verified Lean proofs by combining symbolic reasoning with minimal human interaction. At the core of MathEye is angelic proof checking, an optimistic execution model that replaces failing proof fragments with placeholders while preserving the overall structure of the argument. This optimistic check produces an angelic proof that isolates the exact proof obligations that the LLM fails to discharge. Because these unresolved obligations are often logically interdependent, asking a mathematician to address every placeholder directly is inefficient. To minimize human effort, MathEye performs residual analysis over a proof dependence graph that captures symbol-level data flow in the angelic proof. By formulating obligation selection as a MaxSAT optimization problem, MathEye selects a minimal-cost set of essential obligations whose resolution suffices to complete the entire proof. 9357fef61e96cec2b520d858.title_original: RegimeCouncil: Paired-Evidence Routing For Memory Conflict Governance In LLM Agents
9357fef61e96cec2b520d858.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language agents rely on long-term memory to personalize responses across extended interactions, yet stored facts quietly go stale as the world changes, and an agent often learns that using memory hurt only through delayed feedback after acting on an outdated record. Before the memory store is updated, how far should that negative feedback propagate: should it suppress memory use only on future queries for that same fact (a local policy), or also across other stored facts (a global policy)? Existing memory systems implicitly fix one of these two sharing scopes at design time. We formulate this online scope choice under hidden validity and delayed feedback as memory conflict governance, and prove that neither fixed policy is sufficient on its own. We then propose RegimeCouncil, a lightweight paired-evidence router that retains both scopes as advisors and arbitrates between them online without retraining the LLM. Using revealed comparisons between answering with memory and answering without memory (the no-memory anchor), a Local Advisor tracks the latest outcome on the queried fact alone, while a Global Advisor pools recent outcomes across all stored facts. A Meta Governor follows the Local Advisor by default to avoid cross-fact interference and switches to the Global Advisor only when global pooling accumulates a strictly positive recent utility margin, guaranteeing finite-time switching under delayed feedback. Across LongMemEval

a20d350d06c44b99b4764735.title_original: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
a20d350d06c44b99b4764735.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. This report describes the design principles and systems engineering behind the series, spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training. We study how sparse activation, attention design, model depth and width, and speculative decoding balance model capacity with computation, memory access, and execution overhead. Our pretraining infrastructure builds on MindSpore HyperParallel, combining topology-aware hybrid sharding, efficient distributed optimizer execution, and coordinated management of long-sequence workloads and activation memory. CPU affinity and core isolation further reduce host scheduling interference. Together, these mechanisms support the pretraining of a 285B-parameter model on 8,192 Ascend 910C cards, providing a concrete setting for the architectural and systems studies. For post-training, we introduce TeleGym, a unified agent execution platform that connects execution, evaluation, and trajectory construction to policy optimization. Disaggregated asynchronous execution, bounded oversampling, and partial rollout accommodate heterogeneous task durations while preserving trajectory continuity across policy updates. Together, these advances establish an Ascend-oriented training foundation for the

4150bd4bbfcfac207470db75.title_original: LoCaR: Localized Canvas Retrieval With Frozen Vision-Language Model
4150bd4bbfcfac207470db75.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whole image embeddings can under represent small objects and local attributes that distinguish relevant images for localized queries. We present LoCaR, a training free framework for localized text to image retrieval with frozen vision language models. LoCaR constructs and utilizes independent proposals (SAM2) focusing on the object so as to get a more localized representation that independently encodes each region using the frozen visual encoder. We further study paired-support adaptation as an optional residual that uses matched text region exemplars without updating the underlying encoders. We also introduce LOCFG, a Visual Genome derived benchmark designed to evaluate localized retrieval for smaller and more challenging referents. Across several vision language backbones, our results show that improving the region representation itself is the main source of gain.

a9c09a05fe42200f1ec86b41.title_original: Big Brains, Tiny Board: Pupavision, an Agentic Physical AI Instrument for Monitoring Drosophila Pupariation and Lifecycle Transitions
a9c09a05fe42200f1ec86b41.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many biology experiments are limited by the availability and ease of use of instruments that monitor and record them. If recording stops, the researcher gets a ping on their mobile phone. A simple deterministic capture service records one image every ten minutes and never depends on the agent. We report a 26-day pilot in a fly incubator (about 3,580 frames), including eleven days in which the agent was logged out and capture continued, and a 51-hour outage whose cause led to the layered design. 4e7a8d8de1e52be07658e392.title_original: Long-Context Generation Is a Sampling Problem (When You Turn Up the Heat)
4e7a8d8de1e52be07658e392.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-weight language models are widely observed to get worse the longer they generate. Often, attempts to fix this involve more training. At temperature 2, coding agents running top-p, top-k or Top-H resolve 0 of 100 GitHub issues, while the same agents running top-nsigma resolve 46 to 62 and win every issue the two samplers disagree on, on three Qwen3.5 models. af4341bd6908df62efe04042.title_original: Not All Evidence Is Admissible: Evidence Governance for Tool-Augmented Medical Agents
af4341bd6908df62efe04042.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-augmented medical agents treat whatever their tools return as evidence. We show that this default is costly: medical tools fail silently, and a frozen reasoner cannot ignore what enters its context, so many cases it would have answered correctly are flipped to wrong once tool outputs are added. We call this evidence hijacking. $\mathcal{V}$-information explains the phenomenon: the reasoner has lost the option to ignore, so a tool output can carry negative usable information, and moving the decision of what to keep outside the reasoner restores that option. The theory further shows that part of any filtering gain comes merely from letting the reasoner see less, and only selection by content lets it see better. Every tool output is written as a card that can be checked against the raw input; an independent checker that sees only the input and the cards decides which cards become evidence; and the reasoner answers from the admitted cards alone, with no training anywhere. 43aac964930281295852dcb9.title_original: Readie: Low-Latency Code Sandboxes for AI Agents
43aac964930281295852dcb9.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: From quantitative research to personal assistance, AI agents act by iteratively generating and executing code. To decouple the agent harness from code execution, many agents offload execution to dedicated systems called code sandboxes. However, existing code sandboxes suffer from slow startup. Whether they rely on custom snapshots or a single fat image, the root cause is the same: it is hard to build a compact, pre-warmed snapshot that can be shared across diverse agent-generated code while covering nearly all the artifacts (e.g., packages, datasets) it requires. In this work, we propose learned startup snapshots for low-latency code sandboxes. Our insight is that while it is hard for a single snapshot to be both compact and cover most workloads, a set of snapshots can achieve both. Each snapshot is small, initializes quickly, and covers a fraction of agent-generated code; together, the set covers most of it. We learn this set from a large training workload by formulating snapshot construction as an optimization problem and solving it with an approximation algorithm. Planned on 15K public and LLM-synthesized scripts, our system, Readie, reduces startup latency by 3-22$\times$ and end-to-end runtime by 1.3-3.3$\times$ compared to existing approaches at the same storage budget.

edb012464a706e2af1ea51ba.title_original: Reconfiguring Procedural Knowledge for Compositional Robot Skill Adaptation
edb012464a706e2af1ea51ba.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: General-purpose behavior models increasingly internalize broad procedural knowledge during training, making their adaptation to new goals and skill interfaces less a problem of learning entirely new behaviors than of reconfiguring existing competence. We propose RecPo, a framework that represents skills task-agnostically through multiple procedure views and materializes executable skill sequences by composing stored transitions to realize task-specific changes. RecPo maintains a procedure knowledge base of skill-induced transitions, with each view exposing a reusable factor and preserving local skill connectivity. At deployment, it interprets task specifications through the same views and resolves the resulting compositional queries over the stored relations to bind skills for execution. On long-horizon tasks in an extended Franka Kitchen benchmark, RecPo achieves 91.9% ordered completion with 1.0 ms of task inference per episode across varying procedure support and task-record sparsity. 6d9d2cb1dc607fb80408e160.title_original: The Only Edge Was Memorized in Training: LLM Trading Agents Around Earnings and Bad News
6d9d2cb1dc607fb80408e160.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) trading agents are tested on news, but news reaches stock prices within minutes, and a benchmark that replays headlines at their publication time finds no alpha in trading on them. Money can then remain in two places, before news whose date is known, such as earnings announcements, and after bad news, if the market's fall went too far. However, studies of LLMs and earnings read documents published with or after the announcement, and studies of reversal sort monthly portfolios, so neither tells whether an agent can trade these moments after costs. In this paper, we test LLM agents at both moments on the same look-ahead-free benchmark, before 598 earnings announcements and after 409 bad-news drops of large US stocks. Every input is cut at the decision close, staged agents are compared with single calls, simple rules and a logistic regression, and every decision is made with and without the stock's name. Across five models from four vendors, no agent beat the simple bets. Before earnings, the agents mostly bought and earned what buying before every announcement earned, and after bad news, a Gemini-based agent called almost every fall an overreaction while no agent picked better dips than buying them all. The only gains came from what the models had memorized in training. 163fea246bcfebab2e1664be.title_original: CorrectCast: Selective Multimodal Context for Scale-Aware Residual Correction in Precipitation Nowcasting
163fea246bcfebab2e1664be.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precipitation nowcasting models suffer from errors in intensity, location, and spatial structure. Addressing these errors by retraining nowcaster backbones can be computationally expensive and requires architecture-specific modifications. To overcome these limitations, we propose CorrectCast, a decoupled residual correction framework that refines completed nowcasts while keeping the base nowcaster frozen. By operating on predicted precipitation fields, CorrectCast requires training only a lightweight corrector, reducing computational overhead while providing a unified correction interface across different nowcasting models. Conditioned on the base nowcast and historical quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) and precipitable water vapor (PWV) observations, the corrector selects multimodal context and employs scale-aware modulation to estimate residual corrections. On the Mississippi River Basin (MRB) and contiguous United States (CONUS) datasets, CorrectCast improves six base nowcasters spanning extrapolation-based, deterministic, and generative approaches, with absolute gains in mean CSI averaging 0.0233 and 0.0290 across the six models, respectively.

712df14a61a842fc9bb17636.title_original: RAG in a Trenchcoat: When Minimal Memory Is Enough for Agentic Systems, and When It Isn't
712df14a61a842fc9bb17636.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic memory research has accumulated extraction, supersession, reflection, and graph synthesis on top of retrieval-augmented generation. Across 5 probes x 20 scenarios, no architecture wins universally: atomic fact extractors (LangMem) win rule application, while BRIDGE's block-summary memory wins pattern induction.
